metadata.school_name: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

analysis.name: Alexandrea Ravenelle
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: There is very little graded in actually participation which goes against the idea of a "seminar" class. Most grades comes from out of work readings. She grades very vaguely and harshly. Even if you were to follow the rubric word for word, the chances are you will get a grade much below what you are expecting.

Her lectures are funny, but she is generally a very passive-aggressive and not very understanding professor. Was very disrespectful during Creativity Relay presentations. My group had an issue because a student wasn't doing any work, and she was not very understanding or helpful. The class is easy, but she tries to make it unnecessarily difficult.

She makes her lectures entertaining, however she is really rude and passive aggressive during the creativity relay presentations, obviously aggravated and corrects the content students share immediately after their presentations. Grading is really harsh, its not a difficult class however the grading style makes it hard to get a good grade in class.

Took SOCI89. She can be sassy, and her lectures are somewhat interesting. Her homework is structured oddly, due the morning on the day before class, and the homework was often 25+ pages of readings. However, she is really nice and rounded up our grades at the end of the semester; a big part of our grades is based on projects.

I took SOCI 89. She's an extremely harsh grader, gives passive aggressive feedback, and doesn't provide good instruction on what she's looking for. Homework due before every class which includes multiple readings that can each be 25+ pages. Her lectures are somewhat interesting and sometimes she shares funny stories, but overall not worth it.

analysis.name: Amanda DelVecchia
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I enjoyed this class and ultimately learned a lot, but the class did feel disorganized at times. The Canvas page was confusing and work was returned weeks/months after we turned it in. However, for someone interested in GIS, I would recommend this class, as it covered a lot, and Professor Delvecchia was very  helpful and accessible outside of class

Gave many basic assignments, did them all well. Graded 2 months after assigned, I got 7/9 8/12 etc. Couldn't change my strategy for doing those because it was end of year. She gave surprise grade # of perusall comments we made. Never told us to write comments on all but 2. Got a 14/30 on it dropped my grade by 7% got me a B. Super unfair ridiculous

Dr. DelVecchia is sweet but her class is disorganized and her grading criteria is unclear. There's no way to know what she will decide deduct points for in written assignments. 591 needs a recitation to justify the amount of labs. The pacing and structure is nonexistent, and she is unavailable outside of her office hour.

Dr. DelVecchia is the best professor at UNC hands down! She genuinely cares for her students and wants to help them achieve their goals. She will work with you to find what you want to do then help you figure out how to get there. I haven't has a professor as influential as Dr. DelVecchia in my four years at UNC
wouldnt take again. Lectures were hard to follow. Everyone completed activities at a different pace. Grading criteria for quizzes was unclear. Not enough guidance

analysis.name: Andrew Pease
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took MATH 130 with him. He is a cool and stylish person, but not a good teacher at all. He deserves to be teaching higher level maths and not pre-calc because he overcomplicates simple concepts making it very hard to follow along. I strongly advise not taking this class with him if you are taking a lot of other STEM courses.

10/10 would not recommend. TAs were SO unhelpful and the professor overcomplicates simple topics. I definitely could have done better but l think the way he teaches is directed for higher level math and not pre-calc. He is a very stylistic and funny person and very accessible outside of class with his office hours.

I took math 130 with professor pease, it was terrible. The class itself is not too hard, but the way he explained concepts got very confusing very fast. You have to spend a lot of time outside of class learning the concepts before you can get to actually studying them.
Nice guy who seems like he's trying his best, but the whole class is confused and not doing as well as they should on the exams. I have a tutor and learn from YouTube better than he explains it.

Professor Pease made math 130 much harder than it should've been. The class is graded majority from midterms and the finals. I recommend not taking this class with a heavy course load and getting a tutor asap.

analysis.name: Abel Munoz-Hermoso
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 93 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: To start, I had him for 355 (no option to select that on RMP) Abel is my favorite UNC profesor, this is the second class I've taken with him and 355 has been my favorite class by far. Reasonable workload, he is flexible, he is hilarious, class feels like a conversation, he made the entire class friends and I would talk to any of them outside10/10

Chill and understanding professor. Cares more about participation than perfection, make an effort to speak up in class and it'll go far, even if your Spanish isn't great. Communicate issues or a desire for an extension and he'll make it work for you, if he can tell that you care about the class.

I loved this man, very happy and go lucky, makes funny jokes. He makes class engaging and gives you a lot of freedom when it comes to your written work. Not a tough grader but expects participation in class. You can tell he has a passion for Spanish, teaching does not feel like a chore to him, cares about your learning. Reopened homeworks for me.

i really enjoyed abel and took him for both 204 and 261. attendance and participation are key for him but if you make a good impression at the start and he likes you, he basically guarantees you an A. 204 was mega chill, 261 was a pain due to all the busy work.

This guy is the goat. I took him and can honestly say he was one of the best Spanish teachers I have ever had. If you are a student you need to take him (like trust me). His lectures were fun, although the content is hard he makes it fun to learn, and really wants to see you succeed as a Spanish speaker and in the class.

analysis.name: Aria Tsoulouhas
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took RELI-101 with professor Tsoulouhas this semester and it ended up being by far my favorite course I took. Prof. Tsoulouhas is very kind and displays a good knowledge of subject matters present in the course. She is not difficult to reach outside of class and you can tell student success is a priority. I would take class again with her.

RELI 101 ended up being one of my favorite classes I've ever taken at UNC. Professor Tsoulouhas gives amazing lectures and makes complicated ideas easy to understand with real-world case studies. I would definitely take a class with her again!

An interesting course. I learned a lot while investing a reasonable amount of time. Discussions were also worthwhile. Quick aside: Students at a school as prestigious as this one shouldn't lash out because the professor prohibits plagiarism, or because they assign college-level amounts of reading. It makes us all look bad and devalues our degrees.
Professor Tsoulouhas is very organized with her Canvas being extremely accessible and all of her rubrics/deadlines being very clear. This class has a lot of group work and class discussions.
Be prepared to read.. Make sure you cite every quote. Not a fun class

analysis.name: Adrienne Erickcek
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Erickcek is knowledgeable and does a good job covering the material. The material is difficult though, and your grade comes down to how well you do on the midterms so study accordingly! Still, they are fairly graded and often were curved slightly (including the final) if she saw the majority of the class struggled on certain sections.

Dr. Erickcek is amazing, this class made me switch my major to astrophysics! Fantastic class, lectures, and professor. The homework can be difficult but is totally manageable if you start on time. Having python experience can be helpful.

She is an exceptional teacher, her lectures are so thorough and well-planned. She is so helpful if you make it obvious that you're trying to understand. The content of the classes are super challenging. she doesn't downplay the difficulty. She delivers excellence in her teaching and expects excellence from her students. It's intense, but worth it
She is really nice, gave good feedback on all assignments, but the material is vast and she doesn't give exam practice problems. So it is difficult to study for those exams.
The best physics teacher I've ever had.

analysis.name: Ava Geenen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: PHIL 140: Very nice prof. but class can get dull. Worksheets give good overview of papers but the subject matter is really confusing, especially for your first philosophy class. Half of class stopped attending. Papers are hard but if you go to office hours and the writing center you can totally do well. If you love philosophy, you will 100% enjoy.

Ava is a great professor. She understands the material extremely well and, more importantly, can explain it well. Her readings were thoughtfully chosen and refreshingly contemporary compared to many introductory-level philosophy courses at UNC. Additionally, her unit quizzes required meaningful engagement with the texts, which helped learning.

Ava was caring and accommodated for everyone's needs in terms of feedback and giving extensions. Lots of tough reading but she explained it well in class. Lecture and participation heavy, you will be expected to speak at least 2x a class for a good participation grade.

PHIL140 was an awful experience. The class material felt like a giant circle leading back to the same discussion and topic we had on the first day of class. Paper grading was harsh for the class, and the lectures were very discussion-based, yet dull. Half the class stopped showing up throughout the semester, if that says anything.

This course was fairly difficult for an introductory class and contained a lot of reading and lectures. Professor Geenen was always willing to help outside of class and had some interesting lectures. The material was pretty comprehensive as well.

analysis.name: Todd Austell
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 350 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Todd is the type that believes you don't have other work outside of his class. Of course you need to invest time into chem classes to do well (everyone knows that), but the time he expects you to put in isn't reasonable for anyone that is taking more than 12 hours. Love yourself and take someone else. P.s. he writes his own reviews, so watch out...

The tests are extremely difficult, and the reviews for them aren't given with a key. He asks students to "compare answers" on a forum instead of giving a key to the exams.. He's a caring professor, but his class had to have been the most difficult class I've ever taken at UNC. The final was 1/3 multiple choice with a whole section of short answer.

Todd does care about studentS; however, he doesn't care about YOU- a student. He likes to be liked by all, but is short and narcissistic when it's one-on-one. He also expects WAY MORE than a student can do in a semester and still be successful in other classes, but he doesn't care. Many useless book problems. Final was my highest grade. LOW avgs.
Well definitely a cool guy, he certainly doesn't care about the success of his students. Would not recommend taking his class.

Makes Orgo much harder than it needs to be. Controlling with note taking format, syllabus contains no scheduled list of daily activities, assignments on Mastering Chemistry are put up irregularly, making them harder to get done by the deadlines. Sometimes writes his own positive reviews on here, so beware. Not as good as he makes himself out to be.

analysis.name: Yaakov Ariel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ariel is fantastic! His classes can be hard to follow and he interrupts presentations. BUT! He is a wealth of knowledge and I have never had a professor be more complimentary and supportive of my passion. He can take a joke, is willing to be (respectfully) challenged by students, and brought food to share at the beginning of class. He is great!

Dr. Ariel veered away from the syllabus to say the least. There was a required reading of at least one novel, usually more per class.  The readings were dense, the videos were boring, he was confusing, not to mention the 12 pg term paper. I would not recommend. He was also HATEFUL if you ever had to miss a class, even if you were sick.

I LOVED this class. Favorite professor and favorite class and i'm about to graduate. I would take any class he teaches. It's not hard if you try and are thoughtful. I really enjoyed the topics and Dr. Ariel always brought snacks, which was super kind. For the class, we got to visit churches and write about our experiences visiting them.

Great professor. Provided clear expectations for exams and opportunities to help prepare the class. Would highly recommend any class with Dr. Ariel. Honestly, a gem of a human. 

The topic of 242 (New Religious Movements) was unlike anything else I've ever learned and broadened my understanding of other faith communities.
Great professor, gets to know his students, very personable. Would recommend him to anyone.

analysis.name: Anna Curtis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 203 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I am not joking when I say she is likely the worst professor in the chemistry department. During her lectures, she repeats the same idea numerous times and takes forever to finish simple problems that anyone in the class would understand. If you are taking Chem102, take it with any other professor who doesn't waste their students' time.

The UNC chem department is tough, but Dr. Curtis does a great job teaching students the content needed to pass exams, and she does so in a way that is easier to understand than the textbook. Dr. Curtis is also a friendly person, and it is clear that she wants her students to succeed. Definitely take with Curtis if you can!

If you are a pre-med and thought this course was difficult, you should take a step back and reconsider your long-term goals. This class is by far one of the easiest STEM classes you will take. If you got anything below a B+ and are not 100% sure if becoming a doctor is what you want to do, drop medicine now. It is easier to pivot early on.

Prof Curtis is a great lecturer! She is engaging and kind. When she explains things she shows her thought process so you get a better idea of how to approach the problems. An A is achievable if you put in the effort.
My advice:
1) Read chapters to understand, and put what you're learning in the context of what you already know
2) Go to CHEMPossible

I would say Anna Curtis is one of the best Chem 101 lecturers. She seems to really care about the subject matter and is enthusiastic while teaching, without being too overboard. Although chem 101 is a flipped classroom format which can be somewhat difficult, I feel like she addresses all difficult content and allows time for questions always.

analysis.name: Benjamin Musachio
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I could genuinely listen to Professor Musachio talk for hours. He is knowledgeable and I found his lectures effective at conveying important connections. I found it amusing that he maintains a mysterious air around his background. This was a seminar, so readings and participation were most important, but he also gave several writing assignments.

I really enjoyed Professor Musachio's class. I initially chose the class because I thought it would be easy but it was a lot of reading and required a lot of participation (speaking up in class). However, even as a stem major, it was more enjoyable than I thought. Musachio is so passionate and you can see it in his lectures. Would recommend

Professor Musachio is an excellent teacher. He's pretty traditional in his teaching methods, but makes every lecture fun and interesting. His class has A LOT of reading but it can be pretty interesting and its all important things to know. The discussions are based on the readings and he has a few quizzes, a midterm paper, and the final.

There was a lot of readings to do outside of class, which weren't always enjoyable to parse, and were mostly philosophical. However, if you enjoy reading, want to improve your critical thinking, and like big class discussions (which could sometimes get off topic), then this is a really good class to take.

Professor Musachio is overall an extremely caring and passionate professor, and very knowledgeable about many different realms of literature. The class itself wasn't too difficult, although there was a fair amount of reading. Would definitely recommend if you are interested in American literature and/or political science.

analysis.name: Sarah Bloesch
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If you're taking this for a Gen-ed, I recommend! She was very nice and the class was pretty easy. Lectures could be kinda boring and readings were long, but she went over them. She gives a clear study guide over the midterm, 3 essays with clear rubrics, and weekly reading quizzes. Just wish the TA gave more feedback on assignments.

Super caring professor! Easy class, just don't be rude and occasionally add something to conversations. The tests were pretty easy, essay-style but she gives you some possible prompt beforehand so you can prepare. Recitations were basically just a rant sesh about the current state of feminism and women so honestly super fun class
She makes the lectures interesting and is very understanding as long as you communicate. Love her as a professor, I highly recommend!

I enjoyed this class Professor Bloesch is great and very knowledgeable. She prepares you very well for all the assignments she expects of you. There is a lot of reading but you can get away without doing it because she goes over it during class. There is a recitation which is mandatory but not too much work overall.

Professor Sarah Bloesch is an outstanding educator! Her Sexuality and Salvation class in Women and Gender Studies was engaging, thought-provoking, and eye-opening. She fosters an inclusive environment and encourages deep discussions on complex topics. Her teaching style is clear, passionate, and approachable. One of the best professors I've had!

analysis.name: Bryn Werley
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: CHEM 101 is standardized but Werley does a good job of getting through the topics.  She is very concise, gets the point across, and consistent every lecture. She was very engaging for an 8 am class and would start the morning with a cat picture or a meme. Sit in the front where you can ask questions during practice problems.

Even though I am having to retake CHEM 101, that is not a reflection of Professor Werley. She is incredibly encouraging and kind. I constantly find myself remembering things she said during lecture that are finally clicking now. Professor Werley truly cares about her students, and I am very grateful to have had her as a professor.

no matter what Chem101 class you take they are all the same. Werley was more on track with lesson plans, but she often rushed through it. If this is your first time taking chem ever (i never took chem in hs ) UNC chem is really hard.... I got weeded out! Read, go to tutoring, dont cheat on smartworks. The actual exam is 2x harder than the practice.

It isn't the professor that is hard, but rather the content and class itself. A fast paced class, and heavy on content. Tests are extremely challenging, and weigh heavy into your grade. It is nice to have a recitation to talk things through. Professor was easily accessible and willing to meet outside of class time to go over study habits, etc.

Chem 101 is a standardized course, so it doesn't matter which professor you take, but Werley is pretty good. In her lectures, she often goes into detail and asks for questions from people. Chem 101 is a hard course - I recommend finding another student who has already taken the course and asking for advice on studying, you're going to need it.

analysis.name: Barbara Entwisle
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Her tests are incredibly difficult, and large portions of your grade rely on group projects. I HATE the way she organizes her canvas. Arguably the most engaging and easy to understand class of the semester was the day our TA taught the lesson. Also 2 points are taken off your semester grade for every class you miss starting day one. Good otherwise.

Prof. Entwisle is nice, but she will get mad if ur on ur phone. The class is okay, basically one big group project the whole semester and the grading criteria for it is unclear, and if u miss a class its 2 pts off ur overall grade. It was not hard to get a B+ or an A, but only take this if ur interested in the subject, or ur gonna be really bored.

2 tests, 4 individual assignments, and 4 group assignments ending with the final research project. Tests were moderately difficult; use flashcards for vocab and practice quizzes for question style. Focused mostly on application. No final, just comment on other projects. Great instructor, super experienced and friendly if you showed you cared.

Barbara is VERY knowledgeable, but she occasionally was condescending when speaking to students. Her feedback was great and fair, but sometimes grading was harsh. Overall not bad, but I wouldn't choose to take her again.

Barbara is amazing and clearly knows what she's talking about. The class was pretty easy, there were clear rubrics for everything, and you learn a lot about research processes. Exams were a bit tricky with vague study guides, but its fine cause you can ace everything else. Lots of group work, so depending on your group you may have more work.

analysis.name: Joshua Beaver
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 303 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Allows you to drop your lowest test grade but if your overall test average is still a 50 or below, you're screwed.

An easy class is not representative of easy material, the same way a hard class is not representative of difficult material. It's clear from these reviews that despite challenging material, everyone is putting in real effort to work through it. The frustration comes from how that material is poorly translated to tests and quizzes. :(

Like poetry, this class continues to degrade any hope of redemption to the very end. I've never had a final at UNC that has felt designed to take the ENTIRE 3 hours, in a similar way to the past quizzes, just longer. A passing grade would be a blessing. They say they want us to succeed, but kick us while we're down.

So far, Dr. Beaver has been a decent professor. CHEM 101 is not an easy class but he's very energetic and wants everyone to succeed. He usually explains everything clearly and also gives you time to process and understand the chemistry problems that are done in class. As long as you continue to study consistently and do the HW you should be fine.

Verily, this course is no mere pursuit, but an odyssey of torment where only the steadfast glimpse enlightenment. The lecturer bestows knowledge in fire and fury, yet we, mere mortals, are left scorched, grasping at fleeting truths. My soul writhes beneath this incantation of madness! And yet, is not true wisdom born from suffering?

analysis.name: Rachel Baum
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Decent professor for a decent class, very much focused on developing industry knowledge and applications for the insurance/risk market. Show up, generally express interest, and you'll get an A if you don't screw up the assignments. Much more valuable for the guest speakers than the lectures. Dr. Baum has a lot of connections and wants us to learn.

Rachel is such an amazing professor. Super knowledgeable in insurance. She will connect you with so many industry people, and help get internships set up. She is a legend. DATA540 is really easy, but the final project was unnecessarily confusing. The part of the class with Steve Bennett was really tedious and boring though.

Super simple and easy to understand interesting assignments, no exams, straight forward lectures, tons of guest lectures from the insurance industry, and I left the class feeling like I learned a good deal. One of my favorite classes here

She taught this class for the new risk management minor, and she is so amazing. For a first time teacher she is so good at explaining things, the class is engaging, the material is interesting, and her and Prof Bennett bring in a ton of guest lecturers. Cannot recc this class enough.

analysis.name: Elizabeth McLaughlin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 441 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: do not trust her, she wont give any partial credit EVEN when you deserve it! i self studied everything for the final and ended up doing well ONLY because of that

While very knowledgeable and willing to answer questions, the professor's teaching style was rushed and felt unfit for students learning brand new content. The homework was very hard and not useful for tests. However, the TAs and ULA were super helpful.

Dr. McLaughlin doesn't follow lesson plans or the syllabus schedule. She puts little effort into teaching, but has intentionally harder exams than other professors and refuses leniency (i.e. dropping the lowest midterm) unlike other professors. She is passive-aggressive about people not coming to class, even though she knows her lectures are bad.

Heard shes great for Math-232+ but do not. DO NOT take her for math-231. Shes horrible at teaching the material and KNOWS it and makes the exams insanely hard that even TAs have trouble explaining the material. Told TAs to "grade harshly" to spite students that didn't come to class. Go to another profs lectures to learn. Take exams when needed.

After taking AP Calc and MATH130, I had a fair understanding of the topics, but after Mclaughlin, I have never been more confused about calc. After having near-perfect attendance for the first two midterms, I decided it was a waste of time to continue attending. She makes new notes for each class period and has not followed her posted curriculum.

analysis.name: Emily Burkhead
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 250 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: The class itself is not horrible, you can preview by looking up "understanding analysis" and practice. Tests decide your grade, not hard if you know how to apply a theorem or prove it. She hates to grade higher for those who improved, and she grades harsh, bonus and curve are almost nothing, I regret taking her hunger game class only for a minor.

Taking Calculus 3 with this professor was the worst experience of my life. Studying for her exams brought me to tears. The test study guides are an extremely poor representation of the exams and she wrote most of the final so her students did bad on that too. Her class average is a C, while others are an A. Do not take this class! Save your GPA!!!

I gave her a 4/5 when I took her for MATH233. That was a lie. Tests and homework were graded harshly which would have been fine if she curved generously. Given what she said is "on track for an A/B/C" after each midterm, the curve should have been like +13% when it was actually +3%. Ragebait incarnate.

Carefully assess your abilities. There's no curve for this class at all. It's the only one among 233 courses that requires a weekly exam. Also, I've seen exams from other sections that had only five simple questions in 50 minutes, but Professor Burkhead's test contained more than 20 challenging and time-consuming problems, with no extra time given.

Save your grade and don't take 381 with Burkhead. Inaccessible and hard to approach with questions related to grading or asking her to explain concepts. Asked her many times to explain the material, and was often met with snarky remarks. Office hours are even worse, as she is not much help if you're lost.

analysis.name: Beatriz Lomas-Lozano
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She is perhaps the most understanding human being known to mankind. I showed up for my interview not having realized there were sample questions on canvas, and she let me do the interview on Friday. I didn't even ask! In a world full of hate she is a shining beacon of understanding.

I thought the class was good for it being online. Obviously learning another language is challenging, but the instructor was VERY kind/open to questions and not a harsh grader at all. Assignments were a little annoying at times, but overall were very helpful for the final, which was not bad at all if you applied yourself

Those who have never taken Spanish before don't take this class or this teacher. She reads the slides and never actually teaches and the worst of all, she will only speak in Spanish never english. Half the time she doesn't even teach just tells us to read the textbook which doesn't help at all. Don't even get me started about conversating with her.

She is very kind and approachable. If you keep up with homework and attend class, you'll do well. Midterms and exams are fair with preparation. Oral interviews and video assignments are manageable. Chapter quizzes in the Alcanza textbook are strict and don't allow retakes, so double-check answers.

Professor Lomas is very kind and will answer emailed questions. However, the class setup isn't great even for those with prior knowledge. You'll have to teach yourself all the information, most of which isn't reviewed in class but is still on the exam.

analysis.name: Brett Whalen
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 87 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Nice professor but unnecessarily tough grader with difficult exams. Not an easy gen ed. Don't take unless you really like medieval history.

Dr. Whalen is a great professor who LOVES what he does and is always happy to give feedback on essays. The class was very interesting and discussion based, but NOT an easy A seminar. We watched a movie and read documents weekly outside of class. Part of your grade is from participation in discussions/group presentations and essays.

So many old, boring movies. Watched about 10 films, no color, silent, 3 hours long, and some in other languages, and most were not great. Had to read a chapter a week that barely related to move. There is a big group project, so hope for good group. MUST PARTICIPATE.
Dr. Whalen is obviously incredibly passionate about the Medieval period and his students. Interacting with him is an excellent way to improve the uniqueness of his class.

Dr. Whalen is a great professor. He really knows his stuff and is very excited to be teaching it. He structures the class so it does not burden you too much. However, the assignments do not have clear grading criteria. Overall, a great class though and I would definitely recommend.

analysis.name: Lorraine Cramer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 74 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
1. She is disorganized--a FACT, not an opinion. She can make things that can be explained in a few sentences into complete chaos and get you more confused.

2. She makes jokes: good ones, offensive ones, and ones that don't even make sense.

3. Get ready to read and watch her lecture recordings. You'll spend tons of time every week on this course.

This class was horrible, even if it's required for your major, take it elsewhere. It's incredibly difficult to memorize the amount of info that Dr. Cramer expects. Her lectures don't help, it's not quite clear what will be on the exams (which are ~70-80% of your grade) bc she's so disorganized in her lectures. Honestly she's not helpful at all

Don't take this class. The grade is based almost entirely on exams,required to write blog 3 page every week he exams require memorizing lectures, the textbook, and Anki material. No study guides.the teaching style made the course overwhelming and hard to understand. I would not recommend this class.

The worst professor at UNC. All she does is talk and ramble. Makes the tests impossible and only has 2 (apart from the final) so that they make up 40% of your grade. analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The professor is very supportive and approachable. He is easy to reach outside class, office hours are helpful, and he patiently clarifies any questions.The course is challenging, but he makes it manageable. Homework is flexible and helps learning, and midterm grading is lenient.Overall, a great instructor and you will learn a lot. Highly recommend

Had for STOR 565. Homeworks can be challenging and are assigned monthly  but graded very lenient. Tests much easier than homework and also graded lenient. Decent lecturer but very inaccessible outside of class.
Took him for 323 and 565, free A.

analysis.name: Tim Flood
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The irony of a Communications professor with unclear communication is hard to ignore. Guidelines were confusing, course materials were confusing, and feedback was minimal — and again, confusing — leaving you no real way to improve. He proudly claimed to be a tough grader. I left more confused than I entered. Would not recommend.

If you can take any course at the business school, make sure it is not with Tim Flood. He is the most arbitrary grade I have ever encountered. This is a group consensus. While he presents the assignments as manageable, he grades with little feedback and a lack of standardization. Save yourself.
Genuinely struggled to understand what was expected throughout this entire course. Materials were unclear, and the grading felt disconnected from any clear rubric. Get another professor for 401.

analysis.name: Jade Fostvedt
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 92 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of, if not the best professor I've had in college. I learned a ton in this class and had fun doing so. This course was also not overly-demanding at all and I enjoyed it even though synthetic chemistry is not my field of interest within chemistry. Definitely take a class with Dr. Fostvedt if you can.

Best wet lab I've taken at UNC. To my knowledge, Dr. Fostvedt is the only lab instructor that actually releases the grading criteria used for evaluating each assignment. This course is 100x better than it used to be, and the pigment synthesis is actually pretty fun. Group research project at the end of the course with a poster presentation & paper.

Fostvedt is hands down the best chemistry professor at UNC. Shes so kind, good at teaching, and approachable. So reasonable with grades and classwork and takes feedback from students fullheartedly. An angel sent down to bring a little light to the hell that is the UNC chem department. If youre a chem major or need to take a chem class PLZ TAKE HER

Hands down my favorite chem professor so far (junior chem major). I love Dr Fostvedt so much. She cares about your learning, is kind, and is very accessible. She also wants you to succeed and do your best. Dr. Fostvedt will meet you where you are and try to help you every step of the way. Truly a wonderful human being--her kindness is contagious.

She is such a great person and great lecturer. She is open to feedback and is very passionate about her subject. By far the best chem prof I've had so far (chem major). She writes very fair exams and gives an extra credit question at the end of the midterms and final. There is also an opportunity to memorize the periodic table for a grade boost.

analysis.name: Sarah Ficke
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She always grades things based off of a scale of "does not meet expectations, meets expectations, and exceeds expectations". Iit is not clear what each of these even means and she literally never gives exceeds expectations right off the bat meaning she makes you redo literally every single assignment. I do not recommend taking this class.

Sarah Ficke is a nice person and typically grades pretty fairly. However, her lectures are extremely boring and difficult to pay attention in. She also doesn't grade assignments on a normal 1-100 scale, but rather "exceeds" or "meets" or "does not meet expectations" which makes it difficult to gauge how you're doing in the class.

Dr. Ficke is super sweet and loves to teach this class. She grades assignments regularly and gives helpful feedback, encouraging all her students to do their best work. The class involves a lot of low-stakes peer review, which I found was great for getting advice before submitting something. Super chill class overall!

Dr. Ficke is very kind and accessible outside of class. The way the class is graded is on a grading contract, which can be frustrating as you can't really be sure of your grade until the midterm check-up and final grade are released. Class can be sorta boring at times, but she is very nice, and there is a lot of time to get feedback in class.

She's a nice person, like a grandma but she's one of the worst teachers I've ever had. Absolutely no form of grading criteria and she has a "grading contract" instead of normal grades. She makes a bunch of convoluted rules surrounding each assignment. Never knew my grade, and she hated giving feedback. Class was really slight, just annoying.

analysis.name: Luliia  Fokina
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Fokina is truly the kindest professor I've had the pleasure of learning from. I know so many people who can say the same about her kindness and genius. She understands time constraints and the under load of an undergraduate, which not many professors do. Above all though, she teaches with compassion and intention. I highly recommend taking her.

I honestly don't know why other people dislike her, she is truly such a good professor, who when you ask for clarification will help you understand complex concepts better. She is really funny and always made attending class enjoyable. Definetly would take her for 225, HW is not that bad and exams are pretty fair.

She was fine and a funny lecturer, a lot of the material/hw/slides did seem written by chat gpt which is a little disheartening but the class was pretty easy and exams weren't too hard if you practiced with the poll everywhere questions. HW load is light and attendance policy is forgiving
Dr. Fokina is so nice and funny. She likes for students to participate, so don't be afraid to! She is a super fair grader, so just show up and pay attention to lectures, and you'll be golden!

Only reason why I got a good grade in this class because I studied on my own. Her slides are not clear and very hard to study from, especially if you miss a class. She also just does not teach effectively and is bad at explaining so it's not really of use to go to class anyway. Would not recommend taking it with Fokina

analysis.name: Mara Evans
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 293 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: She can hold a laser pointer extremely steady, it's actually quite uncanny

Evans will spend 95% of class time putting you in groups with students just as confused as you to discuss questions that arent even on the test. Tests are extremely hard no matter how hard you study you will definitely be confused. I definitely cried every other day in this class. I still have nightmares.

Dr. Evans is a very caring woman and is very knowledgable about the course material. I just found it hard to pay attention in class because she doesn't actually lecture. You're put in groups and she puts questions up on the board to discuss (which really sucks if you're not a biology major and neither are your group members.)

I'm going to keep it real with you. I took this class fall 2018. This class is ridiculously stupid. Theres this childish program you have to use and a dumb amount of reading that really just barely prepares you to get a C. The tests itself are awfully worded. study and forget your social life. Evans does try to keep you engaged though.

Do you know when you think you are familiar with the material & then you take the test and are hit with that "is it A, B, C, A &B, A&C, B&C, all of the above, none of the above" stuff and you all of a sudden are unsure? Well that is every question on every test. She also focuses on only real-world applications instead of test info. Boring lecturer.

analysis.name: Michael Figueroa
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Figueroa is clearly knowledgeable, but the class focused almost entirely on musical ethnographies rather than music theory or history. Most classes involved discussing readings in a lecture of about 100 students. There were only four graded items (midterm, final, and two projects). The class is easy overall, but I found it very boring.

The class and professor were extremely easy, and earning an A required minimal effort. However, the material itself was very boring, which made attending class feel unnecessary and frustrating, but attendance was mandatory and graded. The readings were not required to succeed, and I did not feel that I learned anything meaningful from the course.

Overall a kind and respectful professor. However the course was a learning void: empty Canvas modules or a single link, vague paper instructions with no rubric, and an absent professor during "writing workshops". Feedback arrived at least a month late, assignment extensions were frequent, and learning was nonexistent. Wouldn't recommend this course

Great professor. Didn't take attendance but syllabus mentions participation so still go to class. Very supportive during the research process and wants you to succeed. I wish he would have given more feedback throughout the semester since his feedback was super helpful. The final paper is super manageable if you make steady progress on it.

Like many of the other musicology classes, this class was loosely defined as a concept. Dr. Figueroa didn't seem particularly interested in reading our work or giving us feedback, and a lot of our time was wasted with him trying to figure out what to do. I'm almost sure that he didn't read our final papers before grading them.

analysis.name: Toni Formato
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: kind, genuine, and supportive person who understands the struggle of students. super open about her own experiences and listens if you need help with anything/deadlines. she will sit and wait for someone to speak if no one is responding to her questions but she gives good feedback for any answer. would recommend again and again!

She was a wonderful teacher and support system at UNC. She makes it very clear that she cares about every one of her students, inside and outside of the classroom. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her, do it!
She's awesome!! I love the fact that she can relate to us, since she went to UNC.

analysis.name: Greg Flaxman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I just finished his ENGL680 (wasn't an option here) class and still have yet to receive a single grade. We had a midterm, paper abstract, and final paper, and I have no idea what my grade could possibly be because I've gotten close to no feedback. The classes are long and 95% him talking with no slides. He's very knowledgeable, just super difficult

Flaxman is an extremely knowledgeable professor. The class was lecture heavy but he did ask questions and encouraged class discussions. My biggest qualm with the class was the hap-hazard organization. There were only 2 writing assignments for undergrads but he did not communicate prompts and guidelines well. Still a chill class and Flaxman is nice.

He's a funny and nice guy, but I personally didn't mesh with the lectures. I thought a class about movies would be fun but more often then not felt like a chore. A lot of the papers are a pain to write and I felt as if most times I was just jabbering on to met the word count because there wasn't enough content to write about in the scenes/shots.

Great guy who really knows his stuff, really interesting lectures that are mostly just watching clips. Expectations are quite reasonable if you spend any time at all studying and thinking about the content on your own. Decent workload, but it's mostly films and readings. The TA sections can be less useful, but in general a very interesting class.

His lectures are amazing, he is an eloquent and engaging speaker; as a film lover I learned so many cool facts from him. The class isn't very demanding and if you are interested in film at all is definitely worth taking! The papers are graded harshly, but you have plenty of time. Professor Flaxman is who I want to be when I grow up.

analysis.name: Prairie  Goodwin
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 120 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
Key takeaways so far:
1. answer keys frequently wrong
2. tests on content that is not taught during lecture
3. TA's are frequently incorrect during review sessions. Personally, I think its difficult to study when resources given are so obviously and drastically incorrect. Difficulty doesn't come from rigor of material, but rather these aspects.

The TAs don't know what they're doing but have large egos. Office hours are often a waste of time because most of the TAs are just as confused if not more confused than we are. The professor isn't receptive to feedback and lacks empathy. Tests are long and impossible to study for. Tests are also graded harshly. 

TLDR: Horrible in every aspect

This was the most discouraging class I've taken at Carolina. I felt completely unsupported and often left class feeling demoralized. The environment was unnecessarily harsh, and it seemed like the professor valued making things difficult over helping students learn. This experience made me seriously question pursuing this field.

The ratings speak for themselves. Don't come here rating her 5.0 just because you take 1-2 comp classes and a bunch of gen-eds, and have tons of time to go to office hours. The class isn't inclusive of people with really heavy schedules. Oh, and don't get confused by ratings from past semesters. Find a friend and compare how midterms have changed.

The professor doesn't teach how to write Java, making the class nearly impossible without prior experience, so you end up teaching it all to yourself. Exams are unlike reviews and worth 70% of the grade. Despite hours of studying, I feel set up to fail. I've always loved CS, but the lack of support and empathy makes this class deeply discouraging.

analysis.name: Gabor Pataki
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 117 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Listen to me, save yourself now and do not take this class with Gabor. Although he does seem to care about his students, he gives three midterms that are roughy 7 free response questions each with little to no partial credit. The home works are easy and the practice exams he gives are simple but neither resemble any of the questions on the exams.

Dr Pataki is an AMAZING professor. I didn't want to take his class at first because of his poor reviews on here but don't let that fool you! He teaches comprehensively so that EVERYBODY understands and he just really wants you to learn and feel confident with the material. His class isn't too hard and he's very willing to help. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Gabor is the worst professor I've ever had. He is rude to students and is inept at answering questions. He is unable to explain even the simplest of concepts well and uses an arbitrary extra credit coupon system. A real jerk, make sure to do his way of calculus or you're screwed. If you haven't taken Calc before, you need an outside tutor.

The fact that he has an A- grade is one of the most absurd things I have ever seen. His grading is the most ridiculous things ever and I truly suggest getting out of this class before you even enroll in it.  Pataki's way or the high way. Also do not let him learn your name because he will constantly call you out in class. AVOID GABOR PATAKI!!!!!!!!

I have no idea what the person below me is saying. Pataki is excellent at explaining the theory and helpful in OH. The course material isn't very difficult and the homework is great for understanding the uses of the topic and studying. Pataki seems to really care about students. I would say the course is like MATH 347 part 2 but much simpler.

analysis.name: Grigory Terlov
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Greg isn't bad but his lectures are disorganized i.e he doesn't provide notes but its bc he teaches from the textbook so j look at that. The key to being successful in this class is going to office hours. His lectures are theoretical so it is really helpful to go to office hours to get help applying concepts from lecture. Hard, but def manageable!

while the homework is manageable most of the time, it doesn't really feel like the lecture material applies to it. his lectures are a bit unorganized because he often jumps in without telling us what section of the text he's working from. no example numbers from text. he does all of his notes in chalk, so write fast and never be absent.

His lectures don't really make sense as he tends to go on tangents about random things. When asked what he refers to in the textbook, he says to pay attention in class. This class is already hard as it is and other than offering office hours which don't really help imo, he doesn't do anything outside of that. Would not take :(

Greg is a super nice professor but for an intro course the class is difficult, especially if you are not good at math. He gives past exams for you to study but he make mistakes on the answer key which makes it hard if you are already confused. Tests are a big portion of grade and are graded very strictly, he does give extra credit and curves exams.

If you're bad at math and you have a busy course schedule dont take this class. Lectures are useless and hard to follow. Grading is very specific. He posts study guides for the exams but the tests are so much harder than what he gives us. Textbook is over $100. Final exam is 35% of your grade. Tests average in the 40's he gives a curve though.

analysis.name: Gregory Matera
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This was his first semester teaching BIOL 220 (usually teaches 400-level). Easy to see how much he loves the subject, as he's very knowledgeable. I will say grading and structure are a bit unclear at times, but exams are not overly difficult and come from his class slides. You have to attend class to write down things he mentions. Super nice guy!

Dr. Matera is a great professor! Definitely one of the best research professors to take in the bio department. His exams are fair and he's really engaged with the lectures. The more you engage with his lectures the more you will learn. Not a lot of study resources like other sections but not bad for anyone experienced in bio classes at UNC.

Do not take BIOL220 with Dr. Matera if you want to ensure a high grade in this course. The exams are written extremely poorly and it genuinely does not matter how much you study as you will be tested on things that were not covered whatsoever. I promise that it would be easier to obtain an A in Organic Chemistry.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Basically your entire grade is comprised of exams. You can study for weeks for the exams and it is absolutely pointless because nothing covered in class is going to be on the exam. He writes the exams very very poorly and they cover topics you will have never heard of.
Super nice and funny guy. 3/10 lecturer. Makes content more confusing that it needs to be. Exams are extremely difficult and poorly written. Tests on content that he covered for

analysis.name: Gerard Rothfus
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: HNRS30533—Take this class for Honors credit! Seminar style class I took with two of my friends. Quiz every class, except it's two questions you had about the assigned reading and I always got full credit. Two mini-essays that weren't very hard. Definitely my favorite honors class at TCU so far! He's also just a funny and goofy guy as an added plus

PHIL 163. Super interesting class. Topics include abortion, capital punishment, animal ethics, and procreation. He's very knowledgeable and passionate about philosophy and he wants students to be too. Read one paper before every class from either side of a moral debate and then discussed. Midterm & final papers + final exam (w cheat sheet). Fair!
Professor Rothfus presents material in an interesting and engaging way and encourages participation and discussion.

Gerard is really an amazing professor. He cares about his students' learning so much and will do anything to make sure we feel comfortable with topics for exams and homework. I would definitely pay attention in class and  briefly review topics in your free time, as the subject matter can get pretty hard.

I had Gerard for my first semester and I really loved his class, other than it being at 8 am. The readings could be pretty long and dull if you are not used to reading philosophy papers, but the readings really helped prepare me for the PHIL class I'm in now. He was very caring and gave good feedback. Definitely want to take another class with him

analysis.name: Clark Gray
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lab assignments were pretty easy, but point penalties for tiny mistakes were large at times. Our reading quizzes were pretty challenging, but doable. He is very accommodating, and provides plenty of opportunities to make up points for late assignments. Overall, he is a great professor and this was a very interesting class!

Do not take this class if you are not good at weekly quizzes on lengthy papers. The quizzes are hyper specific and they are not open note making them quite tricky as they are a large part of your grade. The work wasn't necessarily bad, but Dr. Gray is not accommodating or flexible on any assignments.

Extremely picky about grading papers/labs and would take off points for the tiniest things. Also had extremely specific weekly quizzes that were closed note and based off of multiple readings that were laughably long. Kind of nice, sometimes? Kind of also passive agressive.

Do not take him for GEOG120. He is lazy when making notes for class and his tests are way too specific. Unless you plan on dedicating a large amount of time to studying for this class, do not take it.
Pretty straightforward class, interesting (but lengthy) readings and complicated quizzes. Grading was pretty inconsistent, but fair ins ome cases. He did not  fw me but was pretty chill to others.

analysis.name: Georgina  Gemayel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Gemayel's asynchronous course was one of the best I've taken. She was organized and clearly cared about student success. The course was easy to follow, the workload was fair, and the materials were helpful. I'd highly recommend her. She made an online class feel engaging and supportive throughout and gave thoughtful feedback throughout!

Professor Gemayel was a wonderful teacher, i really enjoyed taking her class and learned a lot from her. The grading was extremely fair. If you study and work hard, you'll get a good grade. I went to office hours for additional support with some of the assignments, and she was very nice and encouraging.

Do not take this professor for an easy A gen ed. She is a very tough and harsh grader for a 100 level GEOG course. She takes off lots of unnecessary points on discussion boards and is hypercritical if she doesn't like what you wrote. Presented an extra credit opportunity, but wouldn't give it to me when asked for it over office hours and email.

analysis.name: Karen  Guzzo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: So Free. Literally Take notes and do ur work for a guaranteed A. ZERO flexibility on missing assignments or turning in late tho, so if you do that even once you might be cooked.

Dr. Guzzo is such an amazing woman and professor. Genuinely hilarious, cares about the subject, and tests are very straightforward and easy if you go to class. If you need to take Soci 101, take it with her for sure. Hardest part of the class is remembering to do the reading responses.

She is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. Her lectures are very information heavy but it you pay attention and take notes then everything is easy for her exams. She knows how to keep people engaged and is very funny. Def recommend her for everyone!!!

Allow me the honor of telling you how AMAZING Professor Guzzo was. Funny, intriguing, and passionate, Professor Guzzo was always available and open during class. Her slideshows were easy to follow and informative, the readings were chill, and the hardest parts were the reading response papers, which you could easily forget about.

analysis.name: John  Hansen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Physics is co taught and pretty standardized, but Dr Hansen is very fair and understanding. He is also easy to talk to and get to know and seems like he cares about his students. If you truly understand the material his tests are socreable, especially in comparison to tests written mainly under other professors.
Take this 114 with Hansen; he's the legend among men in the UNC physics department!

Dr. Hansen was great! He made physics easier to understand for such a hard and standardized class. He co-taught my section and did an amazing job. He was accessible, caring, and took questions well. Highly recommend taking physics with him

analysis.name: Jillian Hinderliter
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I thought Prof. H was a great professor who cares a lot about the class. She lectures a lot, but also opens up the floor for discussion, so it's not all sitting there and listening. I thought the content was interesting too. She's a fair grader, a passionate professor, and just a caring person. I met a lot of friends in this class too.
She is very passionate about what she teaches! I loved her class despite it being an 8 am, definitely worth taking. The assigned readings were also interesting and relevant to the lectures.

Dr. Hinderliter is amazing!! I took both her 202 and 330 classes, and she is so knowledgeable and passionate about both. There were a lot of readings but they are skimable. The class was a mix of lecture, discussion, documentary/media viewing, and a trip to the archives. Highly recommend her as a prof!

I really enjoyed taking a class with Professor Hinderliter! She presents material in a very interesting and thought-provoking way, and she encourages participation and discussion whenever she can. The work she assigns never feels like busy work, and I always felt like I could approach her if I had questions or concerns. Take a class with her!

Dr. Hinderliter is one of the best professors I've ever had. She is caring, flexible, and understanding. She is truly an expert and so knowledgeable. All assignments are useful to better understanding the material and she gives very good feedback and fair grading. I wish I could take a million classes with her as I could not recommend her enough!

analysis.name: Scott Geier
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Scott Geier, oh Scott Geier. I love this class and given the opportunity I would take it over again. His assignments are fun and interesting and he genuinely cares for his students outside of class. I've gone to his office hours to just discuss career options and random things. He very rarely gives 100s though, but he is open to working with you.

Scott is very smart in regards to MEJO, has passion,and cares about student success beyond class.121 is not a difficult course within itself, if you were to take him I would just be wary of his grading. I essentially only got an A because I went to office hours for every assignments. His grading is harsh, but atleast he's open to working with you.

TAKE SCOTT. As a student who hates coding and digital media creation more than anything, this was my favorite class of the semester. He goes a little fast, but the skills I developed with AI in this class that he taught us are incomparable, and he's super amazing in office hours! TAKE HIM TAKE HIM

Scott is hands down one of the best professors I've ever had at UNC! His lectures are engaging and his personality was bomb. As someone with zero prior coding experience, he made coding non-intimidating and genuinely something I now love doing. 100% would recommend to any design or interface-interested student.

TAKE HIS CLASS! He is a 100/10. Such an interesting course, and I learned so much. Really accessible outside of class, clear grading criteria, and minimal homework outside your actual project. His lectures are funny and engaging. Takes time to get to know you and actually helped me figure out a career path I'm very interested in! Love Uncle Scott!

analysis.name: Tyson Hedrick
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors I've had for a science course. Dr.Hedrick knows how to break down complex biological concepts in a way that sticks. Lectures are well-organized and never feel like a waste of time, and they genuinely care if students understand the material. Office hours are helpful—take advantage of them if you're struggling.

Dr. Hedrick is one of a kind and truly amazing. Yes - there are only 3 grades. BUT, the exams are very fair. Take good notes in lecture (not just on the slides but the things he says) and put into a quizlet. That's all. Also grades on improvement. Attendance is not required and lectures are recorded. He is 10/10 amazing. Loved this class so so much

Dr. Hedrick is one of the nicest profs I've had at UNC, and his class isn't super hard. All lectures are recorded and well-structured. However, your entire grade is two midterms and a final, and the exams can be a bit tricky. I took this class as a bio minor without taking A&P first, which I wouldn't recommend, but was overall a good elective
Friendly and funny made class very enjoyable. Not very difficult and no homework, grades are just tests.

All of the lectures were recorded and attendance wasn't mandatory. I recommend watching the lectures before the exams though, as a lot of the questions were based off of stuff he said rather than just what was written in the powerpoint. The exams were a lot harder than the practice exams, so be prepared. CURVES HEAVY on exams and the final grade.

analysis.name: Hugo Mendez
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 67 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Doesn't teach anything from the textbook that he wrote, but still tests all vocabulary from it. Exams are way too difficult and harshly graded for an introductory level class. Spent more time studying for this class than for any of my biology or math classes, it was unnecessarily time consuming and difficult

If you get the opportunity to take a class with Dr. Mendez, take it! He made going to a 9am easy. His lectures are entertaining. He is also an incredibly kind professor and wants to see his students succeed. Now, the class is quite test heavy with three exams making up 68% of your grade. However, he gives a detailed study guide that is cumulative.

Prof. Mendez was one of my favorite professors I have ever had at UNC. He kept lectures engaging, attendance was mandatory but he made them fun. Workload was one 6-8 sentence reflection from each class and one 8-10 sentence paragraph from a prompt a week. Exams were very fair and study guide was super helpful. LOVED this class and this professor!

Great professor and cares a lot about the material! Unbiased, and easily accessible. Definitions on tests can be oddly specific and meant to trick you, but everything is in the slides from class. Made attendance required halfway through the semester because everyone stopped showing up. Hard to bring your grade back up if you do bad on a midterm.

He is one of the best professors I've ever had! He truly cares about each and every student. For each test, he gives a detailed study guide with all the possible questions he could give. Have multiple assignments that also help your grade, as they are basically just a completion grade. Lectures are very interesting.

analysis.name: Jingfang Huang
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 87 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I dropped this class on the first day to switch to a different section. I had a very hard time understanding him. I was confused the entire class period. It took me an hour to realize he was trying to explain how to multiply vectors, a relatively easy concept. He also danced around questions when asked, instead of just giving a straight answer.

The syllabus of his 235 is unreasonable. Too many concepts he wants to cover, and there's even not one main textbook but only his OneNote, which is sometimes super confusing. He always wants to focus on something comprehensive, but it IS the instructor's job to lead students to dive into details all the time. Y'all should take 233 with another Prof

For M528. There are two sections for this course this semester. I was on the waitlist of another section for two months, from November until the waitlist was purged in January. So he was the only option left for me to take 528 with. He couldn't rephrase the concepts taught in 383 clearly. Thankfully this course has a tb, otherwise you'll get lost.

His class is super disorganized and boring. Though he makes the exams reasonable and easy, the contents of 235 are still heavy. He always emphasized on 'big picture', which sometimes confusing and useless. Overall, good teacher but not fitting to teach.

Prof. Huang is a very smart and nice man, but is a mediocre instructor. He constantly jumps around trying to cover multiple sections in a day, and gives very awkward answers to questions. However, he is VERY lenient. He let us redo our 2nd exam over fall break and dropped our 4 lowest hw grades which is nearly unheard of at UNC. Overall, he's ok.

analysis.name: Harry Cushman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Only did pop quizzes the first month then didnt do any more, midterm is super easy you study off a jeopardy, class seems so intimidating at first but it gets so easy so quickly, final is not too difficult, final project is super easy you get a 100 as long as you put in minimal effort, be ready to ask classmates for missed notes

Professor Cushman if you're reading this I'm so sorry. I almost hit you with my car the other day on campus. I don't want you to know it was me because you're my favorite professor and I don't want you to hate me but I want to say I'm so sorry it was me who almost hit you. I'll be more careful I'm so sorry. I hope you have a great break!

I don't understand why all the comments are good. Dr. Cushman is a nice person and can be flexible, also knowledgeable about his field. But the syllabus is super disorganized and looking back, I learned zero stuff in the class and really thought it was a waste of time. To do the final project you really need background knowledge outside or prior.

i loved this class and really enjoyed the book. it felt like one large book club! if you are even considering this class, take it. in fact, even if you don't enjoy reading, take it. it was so fun getting to hear everyone's different perspectives and takeaways from the novel—that's what reading is all about, after all!
I took this class a year ago and another class with him last semester. He is very kind and knows a lot about the subject matter. Not too much writing, which is nice for a freshman seminar.

analysis.name: Ivan Cherednik
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Math62H is ridiculously easy to get an A. Material is impossible to understand, but the final is take home and the projects are easy after help from the GRC. Homework is graded but not factored into final grade unless it helps your grade. Ivan is so smart it is mind boggling, however his accent and random trains of thought make it tough to learn in

He was a very tough grader. There was extra credit options on tests, but that was for a reason. Tests were so difficult that he had to give us the built in curve or else everyone in the class would have failed. The positive reviews are from the .1% of students who spend hours upon hours just studying for this one class. DO NOT TAKE!

Professor Cherednik was a nice and funny professor. He has an extremely thick Russian accent that can take a while to understand. He is too smart to teach a class such as MATH231. Had a weird grading scale that ended up making a lot of people have their final exam as 80% of the final grade. Overall, I would recommend with someone else if possible!

Do not take this course unless it is required. The professor has a very strong Russian accent, which makes lectures difficult to understand. On the first day, I was completely lost and could not follow what he said. However, he reviews material for the midterms except the first take-home exam. Later midterms usually have about four questions total.

Dr. Cherednik is a kind and caring professor. Unfortunately, he has a super thick Russian accent, so learning discrete mathematics from him is a challenge. He is very clear about what to prepare for the exams and is very understanding. The class, especially the homework, is complex, but he makes himself accessible and his notes are helpful.

analysis.name: irina kruchinina
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: If you are a stem major and don't have the mindset for creative thinking, unfortunately this is not the professor for you. Dr. I is very abstract and creative with her thought processes. To others, her guidelines appear to be vague and complex, but she wants to give you ideas and creative freedom. She is very caring and passionate.

her speech is very difficult to understand, and on top of the fact that the concepts are all very abstract makes her lectures very confusing. jumps between topics too quickly. the details of the performance requirements are usually incredibly vague and not fully explained until very close to the due date. take this class with literally anyone else.

Dr. I appears to be very caring and kind. However, I was very confused by her lectures. There are 3 major performances, but your TA gives good feedback on how to improve. This class was a nice brain break for me as a STEM major. I still didn't mind the class and would recommend it.

Gave multiple assignments over university mandated holidays, unclear assignment guidelines, excessive homework for a 100 level course. Currently have an A but not worth the effort. Professor is difficult to reach. TAs were the only saving grace for this course

Her lectures can be very boring and convoluted, and she also has a thick accent which can make understanding her a bit difficult, especially in the mornings. Otherwise, you can tell she's very into performance and analysis and if you are too she'd be a great professor.

analysis.name: Iris Fitzsimmons Christensen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Profe is amazing! Class is interesting, and she always engages with students. There is a LOT of homework and vocabulary in class, but the Spanish department assigns that, not her. Midterms and finals are difficult due to the amount of material covered, but profe always helped us with what to study. Go to her office hours as well!

Spanish at UNC is hard, but I would definitely recommend taking 105 with Iris! She's super accessible outside of class and genuinely wants her students to succeed! Be prepared to learn A LOT of content, but as long as you start studying for exams early, you can succeed in this class!
She's a very good teacher and explains tough spanish concepts very well. Her in class activities were always fun, and I've always felt prepared for the tests.

analysis.name: Isabella Hinks
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 80 reviews, fairly reliable
