review_highlights.comment: The lectures are very informative and she explains things very well especially if you are new to the topic. At first I did very poorly on the quizzes but after I went to tutoring with the TAs I did way better on the quizzes. I recommend going to tutoring right when you see yourself struggling and recommend it a bit more the office hours.

I came into this class with 0 coding experience and struggled to grasp the content often. However, the resources provided by the CS department are crazy. There is tutoring and office hours almost every single day (Sundays too!). 

Dr. Hinks is great, and she truly did everything (including omitting the late submission penalties) to help our grades.

she clearly wants everyone to do well in this class. turning EXs in before due date gets extra credit at the end of the semester, most missed quiz Qs often dropped, takes the time to explain things well. lectures can be a bit boring if you already know the content, but she is so nice and helpful! this class is so easy if you just put the time in

She is a wonderful professor and explains things very clearly. This class is hard so once you start to see yourself struggling on quizzes take advantage of the tutoring (this is what I did and it truly helped me). At first, I got 60s on the quizzes and after going to the tutoring with the TAs my scores went up to 80s/90s!

Class is well organized. But, if you've never coded, I think Dr Hinks is not the best teacher. Lecture slides are very high level w/ few examples covered in class. Quizzes are short so if you miss 1 section, its tough to do well. I found other resources to learn the content. She did adjust the final quiz/exam weights, which helped grades a lot.

analysis.name: Imran Rizvi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Rizvi is a very talented researcher and clearly has a lot of passion for the material he teaches. While his lectures sometimes seem a little out of order or repetitive, he covers most of the material he says he will at the start of the year, and his exams are very fair. One of the most passionate and easy to talk to professors.
Dr Rizvi is obviously very knowledgeable and incredibly passionate. He is my favorite BME professor I have had!

Dr. Rizvi is very knowledgeable about the subject. My main issue with the class is the lab reports, about half of them being full-length. I recommend going to office hours while doing them as the TA's will always find some points to deduct otherwise. Exams (including the final) are not bad, study diagrams and lecture slides and you're good.

I really enjoyed this class. He is very knowledgable and truly cares about the class's understanding. The only issue is that the class is somewhat disorganized with timing of assignments, and grading for labs doesn't seem standardized with TA's. If you don't pay attention, read the textbook instead. Tests are not impactful, and an A is 95+, not 93.
The best. He really organizes the class to ensure student's success. Truly passionate about the subject,  one of my favorite professors at UNC.

analysis.name: Inger Brodey
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I would rather retake Gen Chem, pull out my anterior cerebral artery, and lasso a bear with it than take this class again. Expected full-length novels in a week and acted like we only had her class. Gives zero feedback on assignments but continues to grade extremely harshly.

Dr. Brodey was very kind, and invited the class over to her house for dinner a couple times. She was nice to talk to, and I enjoyed the class a lot. She offered good feedback on essays when asked. However, the workload was definitely overwhelming at times. We consistently read 150 pages of dense reading for each class, or watched long movies.

professor brodey is knowlegeable, kind, and accessible. lots of reading, but to be expected for an english seminar, and definitely manageable. her grading criteria could be a bit unclear at times but she's always open to explaining! she even invited us over to her house for dinner, she's super sweet.

Professor Brodey is very kind and passionate, but the workload is overwhelming. Full novels in under a week and long films in one night made the class feel unrealistic with other commitments. Creative final project, but I wouldn't recommend unless you have lots of free time.

As a Jane Austen fanatic, I was very disappointed. I feel like we did 85% of the teaching. We had group presentations where we taught parts of adaptations or extra readings. Also, lots of group discussion. We read 8 books, so you had 150+ pages due every class, which was impossible. No rubrics for anything. Brodey was very sweet, though.

analysis.name: Isaac Unah
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Unah's a researcher, not a teacher. Late to every class, very unorganized, & falls way behind on schedule. He had an obsession with teaching us regression analysis (not in class description). The little amount he did teach, he was repetitive & didn't prepare us for the research paper or exam. We didn't learn for a month once. Wouldn't recommend.

You live by the test, you die by the test. I wish this class had more opportunities for students to demonstrate their knowledge on the law and court precedent. Instead 70% of the grade goes to two online tests with large multiple-choice sections. Unah is a very nice guy, but the laxity was too much. Class would begin far-later than scheduled.

Great professor, is engaging, and passionate about what he teaches.  He is a lenient grader, lets you know what is going to be on the quizzes, and he pushed the midterm back 3 times because the class begged him to.  He is a bit disorganized which makes it hard to prepare before the class. He did show up to the final late because of Canvas issues.

Dr Unah is a great professor. I think people need to give professors some grace. Unah is funny and caring. Definitely go to office hours and get to know him. He also has a lot of connections. If you're interested in law, take this. Easy A class - one midterm, 6 quizzes (drops lowest 2), a partner paper, and final. Exams are online which is nice

I love Dr. Unah! His style is not going to be for everyone, as you can tell from other reviews. However, if you can get past his high level of disorganization, his classes are really enjoyable. He has so much passion for his discipline, loves talking to students who are interested in law school, and is just a great guy overall. Would recommend!

analysis.name: Ian Williams
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Ian is one of the most friendly professors I've had. He engages students with class materials by asking relevant personal preference questions about pop culture. Plenty of opportunities to participate in class. 2 Essays, 1 group presentation, 1 exam. Essay and presentation topics were fairly open; he cares about what you're interested in and think.

He is a great man! In my opinion, the lectures are very irrelevant to the final. Our entire grade was based on 2 papers, a final, a group project, and participation, which scared me. However, he was a very fair grader and even curved the final, which I found to be difficult. Not an easy A class, but good. The final is over 700 pages of the textbook

very easy class and material. for all projects and papers the criteria is clear but the prompts are very open to your own imagination. he's very funny and engaging and you could just sit back and listen to his lectures and fully grasp the course content without taking notes

Ian is awesome - humble, hilarious, caring, and approachable. He deeply understands pop culture across generations and connects it to theories, inspiring us to think about the world through class concepts. He encourages discussion, grants lots of autonomy and extra credit opportunities. Genuinely cool prof who treats students as equal counterparts.
Enjoyed and learned a lot! Would recommend. Curved the final and graded fairly.

analysis.name: Ivonne Chirino-Klevans
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: literally 0 feedback on anything in a timely manner. also her quiz questions are very poorly framed and I don't even think she knows what she's asking on them. Ok professor and knows the material but is kind of just disconnected from the course and picks groups for you so your entire grade can literally hinge on a group at the beginning of the sem

If you read the textbook and study on your own, you should be fine. However, she told us just to study vocab and then only put 3 vocab questions out of 25 on the quiz. Her slides are also very unclear and she doesn't share them. Overall, not very clear or amenable.

Easy class, and is an approachable person in general. However don't even think about disagreeing with her views or questioning Academia even in a topic as unstructured as Organizational Leadership. 

Class is easy for sure. But the value is non-existent. She also struggles immensely with active listening in an online format.

Loved the fun interactive activities we did in class; however, she grades kinda harshly with vague instructions. Gave many groups mid 70s-80s on the final group project, which didn't have a rubric. Class quizzes seemed easy, but turned out difficult for no reason. The final was recycled from past quizzes, so that was nice. try to participate

Ivonne is a nice person, but I agree with the review that said you can't disagree with her or she may take it personally. The course doesn't encourage grasping content but more-so just memorizing vocab. Silly in-class activities. Final project instructions were vague and the rubric she used to grade it was never given out.

analysis.name: Jacqueline Lawton
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I liked Prof Lawton (although idk if she liked me). She starts every class with games and time for us to talk about our weeks. She's also very funny and loves gossip. She did give us maybe 1-3 assignments per week, but I think that's fair for a class that only meets once a week. We also had to write our own plays as a group, which was a lot of fun.

Professor Lawton is the kindest professor I have had at UNC, and she is also so funny and personable. Class is basically just a gossip session with your friends and sharing all your opinions on the reading for the week. It is such an easy A, but also a class that you'll look forward to every week!

Professor Lawton can best be described as angel. She is one of the kindest individuals I have ever met. Her passion for addressing intersectionality through drama comes from a deep seated passion for the topics. This class will force you to think and learn, but will be one of the most inclusive and nurturing environments you will find at unc.

TAKE THIS CLASS! Prof Lawton is AMAZING. She cares so much for her students and her grading policy allows for basically unlimited extra time on assignments and you can still get an A. The assignments are graded for completion and a lot of class time is spent playing games!

Professor Lawton was a fantastic Professor who is passionate about the content she is teaching and is caring. In the course, you read approximately one play each week with about two assignments. These can take a little bit of time, but she is an easy grader. So if you do the work and participate in class you should easily get an A. Take this class!

analysis.name: Joe Telegan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Oh my god this man does not shut up. Overly obsessed with succession (literally made us watch in class for 2 weeks). He starts arguing with students and makes class so boring. With that being said, the class is really easy and he offers unlimited revisions on all work if u turn it in on time. He is a easy teacher but he is just tweaking out 24/7.

Joe's a funny dude, but can be a little difficult at times. Very unorthodox teaching style, you'll learn more about people and communicating than writing. Just relax, and you'll get an A, guaranteed, although not work-free. Don't try and argue if you believe you're  right, you won't win even though you are right. The writing's a joke, but not hard.

Talks a lot lol. Also likes the show Succession. He rambles, so lectures can be boring, but worth it for an easy A. He gives unlimited tries on every single assignment and offers feedback. Is almost always available. Super friendly, but don't be surprised if he cusses.
He likes to listen to himself talk, will ramble for the entire lecture. He will argue with you if you disagree, so often better to stay quiet. The class is easy just painful.

Funny and animated, but somewhat volatile. Discussion is encouraged in class, but need to stand up for yourself and be assertive to get your points across. This is not the best class for learning how to write (and if that's a priority, don't take it), but it is a good class to learn how to make connections. He cares about students' well-being.

analysis.name: Lauren Jarvis
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Jarvis is easily the best professor at UNC. I took her for both HIST279 and HIST340. She is extremely sweet, caring, accessible, and just a wonderful human being. Her grading criteria is extremely clear. Her lectures are engaging; she is clearly extremely knowledgeable and very passionate the material she teaches.

Dr. J is a very knowledgeable and passionate professor, engaging lectures that are a must attend to be successful. Show up to class, take thorough notes, and the 3 check-ins + final are very manageable. Plenty of extra credit opportunities. Very approachable and kind, but TAs heavily dictate your grade. Overall great course, highly recommend Dr. J!

This class was tech free for the first time. It made things a little difficult because she would change stuff based on how we did. In the course we had 3 key term check ins which were essentially our only grades besides the final (which was a timed handwritten essay). I think the course was very manageable and enjoyable. Also depends on your TA.

Genuinely learned so much in this class. Her lectures alone make this class worth taking. The assignments were tedious, but there were only three of them so it was not that bad. If you're interested in history and also need a class that isn't too stressful, take this one! There are also many extra credit opportunities if you're struggling.

She had a no tech policy which almost made me drop the class and I am so glad I did not. Dr.J makes the lectures super interesting and the class often flew by. She ensures you are prepared for the three check-ins throughout the semester, and they are graded generously. Only graded on a few items, 3 check-ins, participation, and final paper.

analysis.name: Jeffery Warren
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Warren has a lot of life experiences he talks about in his lectures, but they are often harder to follow because of this. The class overall felt manageable with the readings not being super important with a cheat sheet for exams, but much of the grading (including the midterm and final) was done by TAs, so your experience may depend on your TA.

I thought he was a strange guy, but nice anyway. His lectures were my least favorite out of the three, mostly because they felt unrelated at times to what we were trying to cover. He opened a lecture with the classic: I'm socially liberal but fiscally conservative. I did not attend when he was lecturing, in the interest of time management.

Interesting guy. The class is very TA dependent as the midterm and final are graded by them. Very fun class to listen to, most of the readings you won't have to read, but there are a select few (they will make sure you know which) that you should read. Midterm and final allow a cheat sheet

idst 132 w/ warren (1 out of 3 profs.) is definitely an interesting class. attendance is not required and slides r always posted throughout the week. loved warren's input on the material although sometimes the readings could be dense.

I had Dr. Warren for labcoats and legislators. This was easily the best class I took this semester. I got to meet several speakers from different fields, all of whom were some of the best in their field. Additionally, his assignments are often really easy, and are really creative. With the final projects, you can really be as creative as you want.

analysis.name: Shahar Kovalsky
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I think Shahar is a great professor but only for the more advanced math lectures. This was his first time teaching MATH 231 and it does show. If I needed to take another more advanced math class I would definitely take it with him. Just not Calculus 1.

He always uses the excuse of having a lot of classes to teach and being very busy to not fulfill the necessary duties of instructor, such as providing support to students in need of special assistance, which he basically completely ignores. It's basically impossible to reach out to him by email. Don't want to take any classes with him anymore.

The best thing to happen to the UNC math department. Keeps lectures clear and entertaining, makes sure he takes every measure for students to understand the content. This course content shouldn't be too difficult, and it seems like other professors overcomplicate. Hoping I get to take another class with Shahar.
Amazing teacher! Super understanding and will work with you. Make sure to show up and participate. Definitely reccomend taking a class with him!

Goated professor. In class worksheets used as participation grade, fairly weighted midterms and exams, lots of homework on Edfinity (usually weekly). Exams after the first midterm are open note, that may change though. Hilarious dude, always knows how to make class engaging and interesting. Highly recommend taking 347 with him.

analysis.name: Joseph Compton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 90 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Curved 2 midterms, then told us we were “cooked” right before starting the final, then dropped the curve entirely. No grading scale, no clear policy, and final scores hidden until grades were locked. Some secret points added to the final after complaints. Grading felt arbitrary, dismissive, and shady. If you value fairness, avoid this professor.

Took him for Calc 2 and really liked him, so decided to take for discrete and regretted it. I know discrete is supposed to be hard, but not this hard. Homework is impossible to do with going to office hours and/or using AI/internet (and even then still incredibly hard). Test questions are also unnecessarily difficult. Don't recommend taking him.

Difficult and time consuming homework, no practice exams or study guide, not clear on what he puts on midterms. Grading was harsh and unfair. He's fine in lecture, but makes the class entirely more difficult than it needs to be. Random quizzes to count for attendance & only drops one to account for sickness, so if you have to miss more you're SOL.

I'm not sure why he has good ratings on here... He is very condescending, which is not a productive enviornment for learning difficult subjects like math. He doesn't give any practice for exams. Also, you can do great and understand all the topics on midterms, but then do slightly bad on the final and it will tank your grade.

He was an alright teacher and was very nice. Homework took a while but nothing insane. Midterms were very hard and did not give study material. I do not feel like he prepared us well for the final. A lot of it was just the class, it was by far my least favorite class. Midterms + Final were 75% of the grade, and no drops which others teach's offered

analysis.name: Kristine Taylor
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Kristine has unreasonable expectations for 102 students, considering this is only the second semester a majority of students are learning the language. She expects us to be focused on Portuguese 24/7 and master new content the day after a flipped classroom assignment is due. Do not take if there are other options.

Taylor cares so much about her students and is genuinely the sweetest lady. You get out what you put in, and an A is easily achievable b/c she clearly lays out rubrics and what will be on the tests. She does not give any more tests than the other professors. Very little homework. She teaches 50/50 Engl + Port which is so rare for a 203 level.

An A is definitely possible and her expectations are clear. She cares a lot about her students and it shows. What little homework you have is very helpful and the tests are not too hard. As long as you put in effort to learn, you will do well. I wish I could take another class with her!
Profa Taylor is so kind and really wants you to succeed and enjoy learning. 101 was pretty easy but I feel like I got a lot out of it! Eu amo Profa Taylor.
Prof Taylor had easy tests/quizes but was a harsh grader with oral and written assigments. Often condescending.

analysis.name: Kendall Thomas
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This professor is a nightmare. She will read off the slides like a robot which are each a giant wall of text and ask the class a question after each slide; most of the time, no one responds, and she just smiles in awkward silence. On top of that, she is extremely nitpicky with grading on exams/assignments and assigns a ridiculous amount of work.

One of the harshest graders I've ever had, and she likes to laugh about how low students' scores were on midterms/assignments. I genuinely don't know how to score a 100 on class activities if she deducts points for the smallest errors. Also, if a question has multiple parts and you get part (a) wrong, she will take off points for b, c, d, and e.

The grading is ridiculous. The graders find any small error, either in the class activities or the labs, to remove as many points as they can, even when most of the class fails an assignment. The professor just reads off the slides to teach.

do not take this class. there are no rubrics provided for the assignments, so u sit there wondering what kendall actually wants from u. u get pts taken off bc ur "not creative enough", "extra code", "inefficient code". they do NOT want you to succeed. everything is incredibly subjective and kendall puts no effort into clarifying her expectations.

Whoever is reading this just know I am being super honest, DONT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER! comp 283/math 381 was 1000 times better than this. If you know the horrors of those class and professor you should know this is much worse. Idek how to explain in words my pain right now, I am crashing out so please, pretty please look for another professor !

analysis.name: Desire Kedagni
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The average on the final was a 72. He refuses to curve anything in the class. His actual teaching style was not terrible, and a lot of the exams reused questions from the problem sets, but the fact that he did not curve a single test with the justification of "if 4-5 people get an A, the grades work" was terrible. The average class grade was a C+.

I didn't like Econ 400, but Kedagni made me love econometrics! You have to go to class, since he takes attendance for a grade and includes concepts from lectures on exams. He's a chalkboard lecturer, which isn't everyone's cup of tea. My one gripe is that the midterms are way too long. However, their content isn't difficult. You just have to study.

Desire is a great professor and also a joy to talk to. He made econometrics enjoyable to learn and his problem sets, although somewhat challenging, are great review material. I would highly recommend you study and understand the problem sets and attend each class since he goes through important math proofs.

ECON 470 is very difficult, no matter who you take it with. Kedagni was a really nice guy, but resources were super limited outside of class. Thankfully, I passed/failed this course because the average on the final was a 70 with no curving whatsoever.
I took ECON 470 in fall 2023 and this course covers everything you need to know about linear regression. The pace of the class is very reasonable and Professor Kedagni's notes are easy to understand.

analysis.name: Zachary Yukio Kerr
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Kerr is one of the rare professors on campus who considers the fact that his students are people with lives outside of his class. He is very willing to be flexible as long as you are willing to demonstrate you are putting in effort to the class. Makes an otherwise really boring topic and 8 am class really enjoyable. I would highly recommend.

If you have the chance to take a class with Professor Kerr, take it. He is a phenomenal professor who is so understanding when it comes to his students and is willing to do whatever to help them out. He is so funny and makes going to class at 8 am worth it. You will not regret taking a class with him.

Honest and understanding of students lives outside of classes, especially for a one credit course. Take this class with him if you can, it seemed he was able to be more flexible with the material than other professors because he helped create the course. Met six times throughout the semester, with biweekly online work and a final group project

Zack understood that the class was only a single credit hour, and only had us do what was necessary to learn the content. I had to meet with him for help with my final project, and I mentioned that I was looking for some good study spots on campus. He took the time after our meeting to send me a list of his favorite places to get work done.

Zach is such a great professor. He seemed to really understand the point of Data Lit Lab and didn't make it more demanding than it needed to be. He was extremely engaging, understanding, and flexible with the class. Overall great guy.

analysis.name: Kristin Wilson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Wilson was a lively professor at the business school who expected her students to perform at a high level both academically and in participation. She is an understanding and kind professor, although you have to work very diligently and have to be dedicated to receive an A or A-. Her quizzes are fairly difficult and should not be taken lightly.

Professor Wilson is the perfect candidate to teach 404. She's very well read and experienced, helpful office hours, and pushes students to think further into hard questions. Everyone complaining in here wrongfully thought they could AI the readings and keep up in class discussions.

This class was interesting and practical. Everyone who hates this class just hates anything qualitative. She isn't the most engaging professor, but our class discussions were interesting. Her other section said that she would trauma dump about her divorce in class, but I never experienced that. I have heard Tim is better, but she isn't bad.

While the other ratings are probably more reflective of how the course was previously, Dr. Wilson is really passionate about the course. While her expectations are a little high, she's extremely fair in terms of grading for the course, and is super willing to listen to feedback. Course is pretty discussion heavy but easier than past semesters. 8/10

This class has a RIDICULOUS amount of work for a 1.5 credit hour class. Final paper, final exam, and final project for a business ethics class is insane. Boring lectures and relatively useless busywork. Only somewhat tolerable now because of AI.

analysis.name: Kyle Cunningham
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Kyle is the GOAT. Its lowkey hard to get a bad grade in his class unless you just don't do any assignment. Just do the work and you'll be fine. Super chill with extensions too. His lectures can be a bit boring sometimes but overall he's a great teacher for an easy A.

Choose Kyle as your 105 teacher. 30 mins of work PER WEEK, easiest class you will ever take, 1 assignemnt a week, asnychronus classes, at the end he lets you argue for an A if you somehow dont already have one. He's also super super chill.

kyle was amazing! he is very kind, down to earth, and funny. he cares about his students and is very flexible with due dates and assignments. he also gives very good feedback and grades fairly. very chill and easy class, good for people who don't want much work to do for their 105 class.
Kyle might be the best 105 teacher. Allows late submissions, easy assignments that take 1-2 hours a week max. Also you can call him Kyle and not professor Cunningham
This is genuinely the easiest 105 course you could take. Such an easy grader and there is barely any work

analysis.name: Martha King
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 54 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Interesting med anth class, only 6 reading responses every other week and some annotation assignments. Grading criteria is unclear and grading is harsh sometimes so make sure to check over work. Lots of surprise in-class assignments so you have to attend every class as they do not drop any assignments.

Dr. King is passionate and wants to share her knowledge, if you are taking ANTH270 after the spring 2026 semester the exams are in person and the classroom is interactive, with groups of four. Attendance is not mandatory but random attendance checks are done during the semester. Overall I would recommend this class and professor.

Dr. King is great! She is very knowledgeable and a good lecturer. The readings for this class were super interesting, and the discussion elements made class engaging—certainly an achievable A, but maybe not super easy. The final was discussion-based and creative, albeit a little odd. I would definitely recommend if you're interested in med anth!

Knowledgeable about the course material, but monotonous lectures made the class extremely boring. She is unwilling to accommodate students who have to miss class for any reason and is not compassionate. Additionally, she refused to round up grades, even by 0.1% to the next letter grade, which discouraged me from ever taking a class with her again.

Her lectures are long, and she tends to repeat the same idea multiple times. There are at least 2 readings per week. There are asynchronous quizzes based on the reading, and there are 6 essays you need to write, and 1 can be dropped. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she includes pop-up participation grades that cannot be dropped.

analysis.name: Lillian Zwemer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 202 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr Z has some really hard exams and doesn't release them afterwards. She talks to you like a kindergartener and her slides are really convoluted. Good enough lecturer, but she doesn't annotate her slides much. The course is heavily credited on exams, and there are a lot of homework assignments that do not always feel relevant.
Zwemer is super nice, and 220 really isn't that bad of a class, ESPECIALLY if you take it after taking 103 with Ott.  Zwemer's exams are much more clear and about Biology than Ott's.

The content itself is easy, but her wording on exams is what will get you. Claims she has spent years studying people and knows what works best, but also constantly has errors in exams. INCREDIBLY passive aggressive and condescending when you ask questions. This class would've been so easy if I had taken it with someone else. Do not recommend.

She messes up at least one part of the lecture in every class, and she requires both in/outside participation. I also disliked how she does not release her actual exams, just scores. Instead, she schedules two sessions to 'view' your exam, which I have never been able to go to due to class/work conflicts. Avoid her class at all costs.

Several common phrases used in Lilian Zwemer's lecture:

"Let me see bababa...... So this uhhhh [insert structure here]'s function is uhhhh let me check my notes..... Oh yes! [Insert function here]"
"What a FUN question! I don't know the answer"
"Mea Culpa, andioop, I made a mistake in my lecture the correct [insert] should be[insert]"

analysis.name: Ted Leinbaugh
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 64 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's highly knowledgeable and passionate about teaching, but he rambles on a lot and doesn't stick to the syllabus. We're still on the reading from the first few weeks when we should be moving on. I don't really understand the objective of this course unfortunately. He's still a nice and resourceful guy though!

I am fearful for all of the young women who are subjected to this man. He feels he is invincible, and perhaps he may be. 

Ladies, please document anything that seems awry, especially if you are fresh out of high school. Parents, listen and support your children. Create an environment where they feel comfortable sharing with you. Dangerous man.

Clearly educated at a British institution. Talks extensively about how complex all of his lectures are but fails to provide any real depth. If you read all of the texts he tells you too independently I believe you would receive the same level of education as if you took this course. Nonetheless a kind man who cares about his students.

You do not have to read much at all to get by. 2 students per week must participate, and the schedule for that is posted on Canvas. He says exactly what will be on exams. Lots of memorization. 1 page of reading notes due per week. Lectures often get off topic.

Super fun, well-connected, knowledgeable professor. Beware, the class is more comparative literature than it is diplomacy. He rewards good faith effort, so stay engaged, take notes on everything he iterates, and go to office hours. 3 quizzes, 10 pages of writing, and a weekly reading notebook. Lots of extra credit for participating in CFED!

analysis.name: Christian Lundberg
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His lectures are very funny and engaging, but he can go off track at times, which makes some concepts harder to follow. His presentations can also be difficult to study from. The class overall felt manageable, but much of the grading (including the midterm and final) was done by TAs, so your experience may depend on your TA.

He's just a genuinely great guy, and super personable. I'm taking one of his classes next semester. Probably one of UNC's best profs. His lectures are really interesting too, he's a great public speaker. I had a great TA as well, and just thought it was a good class. I always attended his lectures, even with attendance not being mandatory.

Christian Lundberg was my favorite professor out of the 3 for IDST132L. The class, however, is very TA dependent as the midterm and final are graded by them. Very fun class to listen to, most of the readings you won't have to read, but there are a select few (they will make sure you know which) that you should read.

Dense readings here and there, but he had the most interesting and applicable viewpoint. The midterm was to define terms, then recap a specific reading for each professor. You get to make an exam aid for the midterm and the final, and they give you the questions.

I took this for communication beyond Carolina credit, easiest class ever. Only 3 speeches graded by TA, and you pick the topic. Overall, I learned a lot and enjoyed this class! No homework other than preparing for speeches. The final was take-home and you write what you learned in the class. He also recommends his textbook but you don't need it.

analysis.name: Townsend Middleton
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Towns was the best professor I took this semester. His lectures are very engaging, and it's accessible to get an A if you attend all classes. He is caring and understanding with all students. Grades are based on a 20% midterm, two 15% tests, and a 50% semester-long ethnography. Totally recommend!

Townsend is clear about what is being graded from the start. There is 1 midterm, 2 tests, and a final paper. Lecture notes aren't posted so even though attendance isn't checked its important to learn the material. As long as you take notes/pay attention the tests are very easy. The final paper is a sem long process with lots of help from TAs.

Very engaging class, worth the hour and 15. Towns is funny and good at explaining topics. Lecture notes aren't posted anywhere so taking notes in class is a must. Midterm study guide but no study guide for the two other multiple choice tests. Paper is hard so would probably recommend for someone who has already taken a college level writing course.

Professor Townsend is passionate and does a great job of sharing information and also fostering discussion within the classroom. I would 100% recommend this professor and this class, I thoroughly enjoyed my experience and would take as many classes with Professor Townsend as I could!

Really great prof and his lectures were amazing - not required but very engaging. The readings weren't really required. Graded by midterm (20%), 2 tests (15% each), and a project you work on all semester worth 50% of your grade. Very good class - easy fc-global, as long as you somewhat attend lectures the midterms/tests are really easy.

analysis.name: William McCance
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Mr. McCance is a nice guy- but if you want to learn stats, I would suggest taking a different professor. He uses the chalkboard- often with illegible writing. His lectures are not well planned, often reads slides off his phone. I basically taught myself the entire course. Exams curved 20-30% because so many people fail. UNC stop making TA's teach.

Easy class if you have previous experience with stats, but lectures were extremely boring and hard to pay attention to. Exams were medium difficulty but get insanely curved, so its hard to get a bad grade in this class. Also takes forever to grade exams. Only allowed to miss 2 classes before attendance deduction. Prof is funny sometimes though.

took forever on grading midterms. made office hours at 7pm to find out our midterm grades and didn't show. he barely posts study material for the midterms. lectures are terrible and he says intuitively a lot lol. he never answers emails even though he says to email him. he cancels class a lot (says he's sick tbf). this class made me WANT to do hw

barely homework, and tests aren't impossible, but he doesn't show up (idk how else to say it) for the last two weeks of school he cancelled basically every class because he was sick to be fair but he didn't even hold zoom or offer alternative ways to learn the material. He doesn't answer emails and is inconsistent w being present at office hours

Canceled classes the last weeks of the semester, gave us our midterm back days before the exam. Notes were all over the place and he would sometimes get his own problems wrong when writing them down. The homework was inconsistent and I had to teach myself most of the material in the class. He does heavily curve the exams though.

analysis.name: Laura Ott
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Refuses to provide a copy of lecture slides, so half the class is scrambling to write down content instead of listening to what she's saying. Exam questions do not test on knowledge of content but instead are written to trick us. Median on the first midterm was a 74 AFTER 10 bonus points were added and 7 questions dropped (out of 27). Dr. Opp fr

Dr. Ott wants you to think she cares. However, that is only true for a select few. Very passive aggressive, not willing to answer questions, not widely accessible outside class, and relies heavily on peer mentors. Beware of "select all" questions with no partial credit and no low stakes practice for tests. Dr. Ott? More like "Dr. Opp."

Dr. Ott is one of the most condescending professors that I have had the unfortunate displeasure of taking a class with. The information of the class was bearable but whenever you need something from her, it always seems like she is talking down on you. If you have the chance to take a class with her, do yourself a favor and don't.

The course content itself is not hard to understand as a whole. However, Dr. Ott teaches the concepts in a nonlinear way that is hard to understand if you don't reorder it yourself. GRQs were a waste of time and lectures could be confusing at times. Pay attention to the lecture slides when studying. She is getting rid of cheat sheets soon - beware.

Does not seem to care about students. Extremely condescending, makes the class more difficult then it needs to be and also takes her bad mood out on students. Content is not difficult, exams are not necessarily hard but they are clearly meant to trick you rather than assess your actual understanding. Voice is really annoying.

analysis.name: Tyler Motley
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Hardly saw him in lab by the course is very well structured and expectations are generally clear. Last lab report is extremely long. Even though it's a group/partner effort, it took a lot of time and is worth a lot. No final tho. Rounded my 92.4 to an A so I am forever indebted to him :)
The grading rubrics is very unclear and TAs expectations vastly different across sections. Labs are very complicated and the workload seems endless.

Of course, your TA interacts with you more than Dr. Motley. Nonetheless, Dr. Motley ran the course in an organized and flexible manner. He operated smoothly during mid-semester setbacks in our research project. Lab reports and research papers are the biggest portion of your grade, but the class is absolutely doable, and there's no final.

Dr. Motley is pretty chill. This class completely depends on your TA though. The lab reports are a pain, so make sure you start early and follow the addendums exactly. The final exam is somewhat rough, but just read through the lab manuals for each experiment and you should be fine. Probably the most work for a 1-credit class at UNC.

They gotta change this up. Writing in a certain font or using gridlines in graphs doesn't mean I dont understand the lab. Really annoying and nitpicky when it comes to these things. If you have a bad TA or a bad group, you're screwed! Just do lab manuals and follow every single guideline and you will be fine

analysis.name: Martha Ruiz-Garcia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Go to class and take notes. At first she seems a bit all over the place, but if you take notes and pay attention you'll be fine. I only used the textbook for the final. If she doesn't understand your question, just keep clarifying. She really knows what she's talking about!

This class had a very reasonable workload, with a quick grammar exercise after every class and one final project. I found the content interesting, but you may be bored if you aren't interested in linguistics. We got lots of good speaking practice every class. Profe. Ruiz Garcia was pleasant and made every class fun and engaging.

I had her for 203 this past semester (Fall 2025). She was extremely fair with grading and was very caring. The content wasn't hard as long as you put in the effort to actually be prepared for class. She is also willing to work with you on assignments/homework. Overall she was a great professor that really cares for her students.

I really enjoyed taking SPAN 300 with her! She is great at lecturing and explaining material, and I definitely learned a ton. It is important to keep up with the textbook so you have context for some of the class material, but it isn't particularly difficult or time consuming to read. I would definitely take classes with her again!

I loved Prof. Martha Ruiz-Garcia. Tried so hard to engage with our class, with songs and fun applications. Very easy to understand. Extremely fair - was late on getting our final project back and gave us 100s bc of that!

analysis.name: Briana Nave
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class has so much random rigor it's not even funny. We've had many guest speakers, all have been more engaging than her. Lesson plan assignment in particular has been nail in coffin in terms of unneccessary work. She should not be teaching this class. Great interesting subject, terrible professor and course structure. Mick A is only good TA.

Decent person, horrible lecturer. Talks condescending at times, gives a lot of tedious assignments that takes up more time than my actual major classes and didn't really feel fun or were related to the course. SOME of the TAs are unhelpful and didn't give good feedback. Made us get a textbook that we barely used. Don't take this class with her.

Absolute waste of time and energy. The grading in this class is a joke. The TAs themself don't even know what they're doing. They take off points for things that are never mentioned in the rubric for assignments. Ms. Nave speaks to her students condescendingly as if undergraduates don't know what they're doing. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Nave was okay, lecture was boring. Getting a good TA was gambling, only Mick A. knew what they were doing. I lost all interest in this class due to the constant passive aggressiveness from a certain TA and how all assignments were just busy work. Don't take this class.

Professor Bri talks to the class in an off-putting way and calls people out for not paying attention. She is very easy to contact, lectures are easy to follow, but assignments are long and tedious. Do not get me started on the TA's. Multiple people, including myself have been graded unnecessarily harshly by a TA, and in some cases they're wrong.

analysis.name: Neal Caren
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 94 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's a funny professor, BUT you will be swamped with work. So many things are going on at the same time in this class (assignment wise) that it's overwhelming. You have a lot of reading to do, a lot of acting out to do, and a lot of group projects. This class is NOT an easy "A."

This was one of my most favorite classes I've taken at UNC. While you do have to put work in in reading, getting to know your character, and writing and memorizing speeches, this class truly helps you become a better public speaker. There is no judgement and the more you engage with the material and design of the class, the more fun it is.

Professor Caren is an amazing professor with such a welcoming personality. I took this course to fulfill my minor, and it was a great class with wonderful people in it as well. We have speeches to give, but the process leading up to the speeches is structured so well that you truly shouldn't feel scared. Take his class, you'll love it!

This guy goes out of his way to make studying for exams as easy as possible and hands out extra credit. Really a nice and hardworking professor. The research applications (8 per class, lowest score dropped) are kind of a lot of work but not difficult or heavily graded.

Gonna keep this short and simple. Prof Caren is the best teacher possible for SOCI101 and if he teaches it, take him. Projects are basically graded for completion and exams are pretty straightforward and if they weren't he gives us points back. Barely studied and got near-100.

analysis.name: Nadia Yaqub
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Proffesor Yaqub put together interesting readings, but was not a great lecturer. She often goes off topic and doesn't get into the meat of her lecture. She also will try and keep you after class is over to continue her lecture if she got off topic. I wish she was a better lecturer because what she has to say is often very interesting.

These classes are not easy, it is very reading heavy and she is a harsh grader. But she really cares about students and is very understanding of any outside circumstances you might have, which can't always be said for other proffessors at UNC. I was very grateful that she was so understanding.

I really enjoyed the class. Dr. Yaqub is very knowledgeable and approaches the subject very well. She is a little disorganized, and the class is reading heavy, especially for the first two exams. Other than that, I enjoyed the class and learned a lot.

This class is really not that bad. It's interesting and I learned a lot. That being said, Nadia was not a good lecturer. She's clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches, but she just doesn't do a good job teaching to such a large body of students. Students should know that her unit focuses on the Israel-Palestine conflict.

She seems to not be open to students perspectives. She quickly shuts down peoples opinons and judges people harshly. She does not stick to her PowerPoints, and instead will go off on tangents that do not relate to the test material. She is hard to follow and does not seem like a genuine, caring, person. I would not take another class with her.

analysis.name: Natasha Parikh
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 129 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: super nice, class was rly easy, poll everywhere everyday, labs every week for completion, assignments every week for accuracy but super easy and using jamovi. take home quizzes, midterm and final. uses piazza for participation

She was wonderful. The course was structured where you watch lectures before class and do some compression questions (but that should take about an hour at most). In class we do review, poll everywhere, and work on assignments, which is really nice because you can get a lot of help from both Dr Parikh and the ULAs/IAs. Overall a great course!!!

Amazing Professor! She made retaking stats an enjoyable experience. The one downside I had with her is that she often would respond to emails very late, and many times she wouldn't even respond. But, it was not an issue as she was very welcoming and always had time before or after class to speak. I would recommend taking a class with her!

She is a great person! But on top of that this is the best class I have taken. The lectures are actually interesting and all test are take home and open note including the midterm and final. The only thing that you are not guaranteed to get an 100 on is the in class assignment but those don't really impact your grade. Take this easiest A.

Prof. Parikh is a great professor! 210 content was a bit dull just because it's statistics focused, but she made it as interesting as it can be. Easy A! Labs are automatic 100s as long as you try, and assignments are pretty easy. I liked how detailed instructions were provided. Overall, take it with Prof. Parikh.

analysis.name: Adi Nester
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Nester is very nice and enthusiastic about what she teaches. She really cares about students understanding the materials. The lectures were very informative and engaging and the class discussions were interesting. Homework assignments were straightforward and most of the time she gave the answers already in class before we had to submit.

Dr. Nester was a very kind and understanding professor. She assigned lots of extremely lengthy readings which were the only things covered in lecture. Her exams were what you make of them, she is very clear with what will be on the exam, you just have to make sure to prepare for them well because she is a tough grader in my opinion.

I enjoyed this class! You can tell Nester is very passionate about the subjects, which sometimes led to going over time with lectures and getting off schedule. She really wants to help her students, she gave plenty of feedback on assignments and offered extra credit. She can be a little bit of a tough grader, but is clear with her expectations.

The class was very interesting and the lectures were well-organized with really helpful slides that made studying for the exams much more manageable. Prof. Nester is very nice and accommodating. She encouraged participation in class and gave a lot of helpful feedback on the homework assignments.

Professor Nester's class was wonderful. We read engaging texts from diverse perspectives, creating a rich and meaningful learning experience. Discussions were consistently thoughtful and in-depth. Exams were fair, and she clearly reviewed key material and how to prepare. Highly recommended.

analysis.name: Zachary Nimchuk
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is super nice and so interested in CRISPR! There is 1 midterm and you get a cheat sheet. The average was a B+ and he gave us 2 questions back that people missed. Otherwise, the only other grades are a semester long group project and the "final exam" which is a prompt that you get ahead of time and can prepare. Definitely recommend this class.

Dr. Nimchuk has been by far the best biology professor I've ever had at UNC. This course was my absolute favorite this semester and I always looked forward to sitting in lecture. He is very knowledgable with the CRISPR-CAS9 system and has so much insight to provide. Everyone should take this class and witness how marvelous Dr. Nimchuk is!

The best professor I've had at UNC. Very clear on his expectations and willing to explain difficult concepts. The class material was interesting for people interested in genetics and molecular biology. If you read and understand the papers, you will do well.

Loved Dr. Z! His lectures were engaging and entertaining to learn from. He sent out a weekly email that outlined the class we had that week and showed how much he cared about us. This was a 1-credit seminar, but he's teaching a full course on CRISPR next semester which I would highly recommend!

Great professor and person. Very knowledgeable on the subject matter and cares about the students. Seems as though he wants students to succeed and learn from his class. I highly recommend his course on CRISPR if you're a science major and interested in genetics. Final project was a lot of fun.

analysis.name: Markus Nevil
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: In my opinion, this class needs to be entirely restructured. Very odd grading system, tons of group work, and zero real learning. Also, zero accountability for group members not helping. Basically, a high school science class. Despite Bio 101 being a pre-rec, we spend time in 105L learning 101L skills. Could be useful, just needs to be rethought.

Idk why Bio105L gets the bad rep. This class was super easy GPA booster. It's the easiest bio class I've ever took. The assignments didn't even take that long either. The only things that took time were the papers. But then again, they were group assignments and u r only responsible for one or two sections. Easy class. No final exam, just a paper.

Nevil seems great, but this class is the worst. Unsure if he set it up or was assigned to teach it, but it's the most nonsense class you'll ever take. Assignments take forever, are pointless, and have insanely confusing rubrics; it's a busy work highschool class. I don't get how this is considered a prereq because holy yap and time/energy wasted.

Dr. Nevil was great in 105. There was a lot of work to do every week but there were a lot of interesting topics. Due dates were clear and easy to keep track of. The rubrics for the projects were helpful and you can resubmit if you dont do well on the first try. Dr. Nevil was the the professor who did the lectures and I thought they were interesting

Dr. Nevil is kind, but the lectures are a waste of time. No exams, just a bunch of projects/assignments. Peer Reviews, discussion boards, and easy online video quizzes. Every week, there's a group lab report assignment. Annoying but easy once you get the hang of it. This class had so many assignments, but easy A. Good GPA boost

analysis.name: John Noonan
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style

review_highlights.comment: Noonan is a truly a kind person, making an effort to remember your name and make 231 really entertaining than most sections.
