Dr. Noonan is lots of fun! Teaching style could definitely be improved, but he's engaging and silly, and answers specific questions pretty well. I leaned HEAVILY on the ULAs in the class to actual learn material and prepare for tests... probably would've failed without them. Overall fun, but you're left to learn a lot of material on your own.

Professor Noonan is a great example of great person, somewhat lackluster teacher imo. He is lively and brings good energy to his classroom. However, his teaching is not my cup of tea. The material that is on exams is very different from what's practiced on homework/class. It was often "figure it out" with not much else for help. I felt unprepared.

Professor Noonan was such a great person and I enjoyed having him but the class itself was not the best. He was very all over the place and felt like we didn't have enough time to do anything. He is new though, so I think he's just getting the hang of thing and hopefully future classes will be more organized. I had to teach myself most material :(

I really like Noonan as a person and he wants the best for his students, his only down fall is the lectures. He gives a worksheet to work through and just gives the answers at the end of class. This was his first semester teaching here, so he was figuring out what worked along the way, so hopefully future classes will have more productive lectures.

analysis.name: Katherine Newhall
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Nice person, horrible professor. Can't lecture/teach for the life of her, tests have material that were never covered during lectures. Doesn't know what she's doing (didn't create class material, didn't create homework, lectures like she went over the slides the night before) and is only available two days of the week.

Honestly maybe not her fault since this is her first time teaching this course but awful. Did not teach half of exam 2 and has not curved it. Very disorganized, not responsive, overall just a difficult class. Self taught most of the material bc lectures were insufficient leading to poor grades. Avoid!!

This class feels hard if only listening to lecture, but if you keep track of the homework and try to really understand the material getting at least a B+ is def doable. Professor Newhall might not be the best lecturer but she's a really nice person, and she gave out curve at the end which makes 92.9 an A and 89 and A-.

DO NOT TAKE, never have I struggled in math as hard as in MATH-235. Never taught the class before so she could not do half of the problems in lectures. The tests are hard. They usually do not include the material given in the review sheets. The final had no review material, topic lists, etc. The labs aren't helpful.

Math 235 isn't an easy A and lectures can be hard to follow, but Professor Newhall is very responsive and gives a generous curve. The class is test-heavy, yet the exams are fair and one midterm can be replaced by the final. She also offers grade boosters like lab attendance and worksheets, though labs aren't very helpful, and grading varies by TA.

analysis.name: Nora Hanagan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof Hanagan is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter, and she heavily encourages participation. She's a relatively tough grader as far as first year seminars go, but if you do the readings and put in some effort, you should be fine. The major grades are an in-class debate, short video, two reading analyses, and an oral exam.

Awesome professor, not too difficult. HEAVY readings and has textbooks, but can probably get PDFs. Main grade is a debate which needs a fair amount of effort but she gives class time, groups are random but worked out pretty well for our class. Fair grader, just put effort into your papers and reflections and in class writings and you'll do fine.

I liked this class. Lots of reading some required for in class assignments. She's a great lecturer so it made a class I was worried about more digestible. There's a debate at the end of the semester you might be worried about but it was pretty easy. Not a harsh grader either

I like her a lot, she is very sweet and caring. Flexible with attendance if you have a genuine reason you can't be there. her lectures are sometimes quite dry. Class involves a lot of group discussion so do the readings.

Dr. Hanagan is incredibly knowledgeable about American political theory and delivers lectures in a way that make the content digestible. There is a significant amount of content covered, so I would recommend doing all the readings if you want an A. She is accessible and helpful in office hours. Overall, I learned a lot and improved as a writer.

analysis.name: Todd Ochoa
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 79 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Todd was a enthusiastic lecturer but sometimes did not explain the material in the readings well. There were lots of readings in this class - some of them were very dense. My TA broke down the material into manageable chunks that Todd lacked in lecture. Only 2 papers but weekly small writing assignments. Very low stress!

Passionate and caring professor. The small group oriented lessons implemented for this semester were a miss (especially if you're anxious speaking in a massive class hall). Class attendance is graded but may be *ahem* bypassed relatively easily with the check-in beacon system. Lots of homework is assigned, but was ungraded and therefore optional.

Awesome professor. Really knows what he's talking about is my favorite type of nerd/geek. He really does make the class engaging and provides nice discussions in class. There is a lot of material you need to read, however Ochoa does clarify ideas and concepts from them in his lectures. I would highly suggest taking this professor.
Lots of reading and writing and the contents feel super boring and dense. Plus, this class has high threshold (95%) for getting an A. Take this class if you truly enjoy religion.

Ochoa is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. Lectures were amazing and extremely interesting, class was fun and interactive. He makes very deep topics about religion and society very accessible to people of all backgrounds. I'm a CS major and Todd made me want to add a RELI minor. Not that hard if you just do the work and skim the readings.

analysis.name: Michal Osterweil
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. O is odd, but I do recommend her because she'll change the way you look at the world forever. This class can be frustrating at times in the way that's like those tiktoks where the girl is like "when a man has a thought I had when I was 7," but don't take it to heart if she comes off as patronizing because she really does just want you to learn.

Dr. O is a genuinely good person who cares about the class, her students, and the content. This being said, the class is semi-disorganized and can be redundant. Lots of reading, but you only really need to do it if you're doing the reading responses. Pretty liberal and not very open to other perspectives, so prepare accordingly. Go to office hours!

Dr. O is a great professor! The class itself was honestly not too bad, you just have to keep up with some readings (and you can honestly get away with not doing a lot of them). The tests were mostly short response with some multiple choice, but Dr. O and the TAs grade pretty leniently. Overall, fun and straightforward class!

We meditated before each class, which was kind of cool in my opinion. The course material is interesting and progressive, if you're into that stuff. The papers and exams were graded very leniently. If you can showcase within them that you did the readings / kept up with class, you will do very well. Attendance is not mandatory, but I recommend it.

Dr. Osterweil's class was definitely the most unique I've ever taken really - it is obvious she cares about the material very deeply and really gets you thinking. Even though the class could've been a bit more organized and straightforward, I really enjoyed the energy and knowledge she brought to the course. She's also very kind, open, and driven.

analysis.name: Mike O’Sullivan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. O'Sullivan is my favorite lecturer at UNC. He is passionate and pretty funny, although self-deprecating at times. I liked learning how history is still very relevant today in stuff like politics. Few assignments, and most are completion/effort. There is a lot of reading, but take the time to go thru everything to ace the midterm and final.

Professor O'Sullivan gave detailed lectures and made sure to show every side of the various historical debates that we covered throughout the course. He provides good feedback on writing for history and is willing to talk and answer questions outside of class in general. He is very smart but also very down-to-earth, and kind to students.

Heavy on the reading, but very entertaining lectures, talks as if he is telling a story and is easy to learn from. Easily accessible outside class, very kind and very understanding. Encourages people with no outside knowledge to take the class. Highly recommend.

Hard to take notes on his lectures, it's a LOT in a short class period. Very story telling adjacent, so he's fun to listen to if you enjoy the topics. Amusing, very caring, chill professor. Very understanding. Graded on midterm paper and final paper, and a few reader response. Lots of reading and one group presentation.

Professor O'Sullivan is so nice! The course is easy overall: 3 reader responses, a map quiz, a mid-term, and a final exam. Don't stress if you are struggling, go to his office hours and he's always willing to help. This course is reading heavy and quite fast paced, so make sure you do your readings or else you'll feel lost in class

analysis.name: Mariana Olvera-Cravioto
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It's undeniable she is a great person passionate about the subject and accessible outside the classroom. However I would not recommend taking this if you don't have background in stats or math. The lectures are extremely confusing and require you to know the material beforehand. Hardest tests ever. If you take 435 with her good luck you'll need it.

Lower averages than other sections. Failed several of her students. Insufficient prep materials for the exams. No recorded lectures. Exams were much more challenging than other sections. Homeworks take a ridiculous amount of time to complete. Professor has been falsely represented in her ratings. You've been warned. No curves when over half fail...

I had her for 435 and 445. I really struggled through 435 and her lectures started getting pretty confusing, but shes still an amazing prof and person. I'm half way through 445 right now and I do think it's a lot easier than 435 and I am enjoying my second class with her a lot more than my first.

To be honest I did not know what to expect with a 400 level class called Introduction to Probability but it was like two weeks of introduction. PSA that you need to do calculus in this course and I spent like 14 hours a week on this class. Go to class and do extra practice problems because honestly understanding the question is half the battle.

This was by far the hardest class I have ever taken. The exams were very hard and you needed to study for two weeks to just pass the exams. Mariana however is accessible outside of class and wants to help. Just know if you plan on taking this course, buckle up. Originally, I had a D but my final grade was "curved" to a B so that slayed.

analysis.name: Barbara Osborne
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Overall, a good professor but the class material is boring, it's based around a lot of readings and court cases, so she can only make it so interesting. The quizzes online for each chapter can be difficult but are not too hard if you go to class and pay attention. Quizzes could probably be done w/o going to class but would definitely be harder.

I took her EXSS326 summer class and she rocks. She's really funny and gets to know all her students really well. She tells personal stories related to the law that are actually interesting, and she will help you out if you're ever confused or having trouble with anything. Participation is a big part of her class.
Not an easy course, but with 100% online quizzes you can do well on them. Attendance is optional and overall just boring lectures.

You will not regret taking Professor Osborne! She is hands down one of the best professors I have ever had the privilege of taking. I highly recommend her course and she will always do whatever it takes to make you successful in the course. She definitely cares about her students. The course has challenging aspects of it as it is a law class.

I loved Prof. Osborne! Truly caring for her students. Her 326 class is graded 85% on open-book, open note quizzes and 15% class participation, so doing well on the quizzes really matters. I was having trouble with the quizzes for the first part of the semester and started emailing her specific quiz questions and it saved my grade. So helpful!

analysis.name: Timothy Ott
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Attendance played a big role in grading. Students were often asked to upload photos, which were then used to track attendance. The class felt quite boring, relied heavily on cold calling, and the slides were very amateur and could be much better. Overall, grades seemed to be based more on attendance than on actual learning or engagement.

Long cases and a quiz required for every lecture, were just a large amount of time and super exhausting. Ott is a good lecturer, however, the final project (which is a presentation) is a large amount of time and the average for the final project was a 75. I felt like it was hard to know what he was looking for since the TA graded our quizzes

I personally like Prof Ott, but know others who didn't. He's a tough grader, good lecturer and a nice guy. This course is based on 9 case studies with quizzes on each and a final group project. Grade-wise, it's 30% - Participation, 40% - Quizzes, 30% - Group Project. This class has a lot of reading, and if you do it, you'll do well.

analysis.name: Matthew Owain
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He sent me this email without knowing I am mentally ill and have been struggling with school. "I noticed that you were absent on the first day. Please drop as soon as you can. As policy, I do not over-enroll and the waitlist is 18 people deep and I am sure others would love to join this class." I dropped because of this. I found this to be rude.

I took this online/asynch over the summer and it was just okay for if you want to actually improve your writing. Not much work, easy for a quick credit or A. His videos were short, simple, & a bit awkward. He gave basically no feedback (it all came from our group mates) and the canvas was a mess. Decent bit of reading followed by peer discussions

Prof Owain is amazing, super enthusiastic and cares a lot about students. He fosters a safe environment in class and makes students feel comfortable sharing their thoughts. The assignments are really enjoyable and you edit them as a small group with peers. Pro Owain gives incredibly thoughtful feedback and is all around great, cannot recommend more

Very chill professor, highly recommend taking a class with him. Participation matters a lot, but it is easy to talk in class. Three papers and one final group project. He cares a lot and wants to see you succeed!

Take Professor O'wain! In ENGL 138, there were 3 easy papers, 1 final group project, and participation (30% of grade but just talk once or twice a class you will be fine). I enjoyed coming to class everyday and highly recommend taking any class you can with Professor O'wain!

analysis.name: Max Owre
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I am someone who loves all of my history classes. However, this was unlike any course I have taken prior (of which there are many). Grand total of 2 assignments graded by LDOC, insanely tough grader (free write exams - 45 min only), and unclear grading criteria. I literally had nightmares about these exams and almost didn't make it out alive.

Max gets so disorganized that it's hard to understand the point of the lectures. He gives no context for a lot of it, ultimately making it hard to understand for a beginning history class. All of the grades are based on the TA's, so you better hope you get a good one. I felt like getting an 'A' was practically impossible, even while going to hours.

Professor Owre was definitely very nice but the damage that I think is about to occur to my GPA is a major thorn in my side. Although that is mostly due to me TA (who pains me even more), the way the class was structured didn't help much either. Essentially, unless you're purely interested in the topic, I wouldn't take this course.

I feel set up for failure in this class. I want to stay on top of the readings, but he doesn't post them for class ahead of time or even for weeks after the fact. Also, engaged activity reports  dumb. I go to every class and recitation, but still think the best possible grade I can get is a B. I feel like I work so hard but it doesn't even matter.

I wanted to like Max and this class but I just couldn't. His lectures are overly verbose and since he slacks on posting the readings, I was constantly confused about the material. It is obvious that his other job, exec. director of Carolina Public Humanities, is his priority and he doesn't make enough time to be an organized/effective professor.

analysis.name: Oluremi Abayomi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 115 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Beware of this class! It is insanely challenging for an intro-level course. There are no HW/lab drops or curves. You could be on your deathbed and Dr Remi still would not give you an extension. Never answers emails and talks down to you during office hours and when asking questions in class. Goes indepth on easy concepts, but breezes by hard ones.

This class and Professor Abayomi's teaching was not very intuitive for someone who doesn't have any coding/limited stats experience. It isn't necessarily extremely challenging, but I would recommend taking this class when you have a lot of time to rewatch Abayomi's lectures and dedicate to the labs. He is funny and friendly, but pretty strict

The class itself is useful, but the grading was unnecessarily nit-picky. The professor was egotistical and unwilling to answer any questions or provide any sort of help. They spoke with an air of superiority and disrespect that I've never received from any other human being. I've never cried so much over a class. Do not take this class.

This class is just a cheap knockoff of UC Berkeley's Data8—he's stealing their work word by word and claims it as his own. At times he would switch the states from CA to NC to not make it as obvious. If you want to get a feel of how the class would be I encourage you to look it up, and practice. You'll pass the class with flying colors!

Dr. Remi was a very thorough teacher but was very condescending as a professor. He had very little patience and was rude to students on occasion. While his lectures were thorough, he spent a lot of time explaining simple concepts that everyone already knew.

analysis.name: Petal Samuel
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: super chill and actually very interesting class. you get 7 unexcused absences and your entire grade is just a bunch of little discussion posts. there is a group project but its not hard at all. you would literally have to try mega hard to not end with an A. Professor Samuel was incredibly kind and engaging.

Dr. Samuel is an amazing professor. She is very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. Everything she assigns is discussed in class, so you do not forget. I enjoyed how every topic was discussed in class, making it easier to understand the concepts being taught. I 100% recommend her and would take another class with her.

Dr. Samuel is an incredible professor! I truly looked forward to her classes every week. The content was very intentional and well-planned out. Her instructions were always clear and she was very accessible in person or via email. I would highly recommend taking a class with her if you can! 10/10 recommend!
No exams which is amazing. You are allowed to miss up to 7 classes with no penalty so super lenient. 2 group projects and mini reading quizzes. super easy class and sweetest professor.

Genuinely Dr. Samuel made class great and really cared about student feedback for her course when it came to the low amount of homework that was assigned. She is really understanding when it comes to being absent or needing to use an extension. As long as you communicate with her, her class is great and very interesting/informative!

analysis.name: Pamela Bond
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bond made learning a joy. She is by far the most kind and energizing professor that I have experienced. She always showed up to class with a smile and was the highlight of my day. Her assignments consisted of reflective essays, designing our own sustainable fashion piece, etc. I learned a lot and had a bunch of fun in the process!

Professor Bond is the best teacher I have had at UNC so far. She genuinely cares for all her students and she gives you the confidence to participate. She is hilarious and  I always leave class feeling so much better than I did walking in. All the assignments are easy but interesting and you learn so much from her style of teaching!

Pamela Bond is such an incredible teacher and even better person. She's super understanding and clearly cares more about you learning than busy work. Would recommend you take her classes, but if you do, please give her the respect and attention she deserves!! Top tier teacher!

Professor Bond is probably one of the (if not the) best teacher I have ever had. Not only will you leave her class laughing, but you also feel as if you have a genuine friendship with her. Her lectures are very interesting and taught in a very entertaining way. You will not regret taking her class.

Professor Bond was one of the best professors I have ever had in college. She was so caring and made class so engaging and fun. She genuinely sparked interest and inspired me every single day. I cannot emphasize enough how awesome she is and how awesome this class is. Shes truly the best.

analysis.name: Peter Doyle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's fine but try to get another 121 teacher if you can. He has no clear grading criteria at all and will take off points differently for each student depending on how he's feeling...I tried to talk to him about a grading concern I had and he responded with very rude emails. Definitely have to teach yourself all the coding and video editing too.

Peter can be hard to reach outside of class sometimes. While other times he is quick to respond. I guess it depends on his mood. Extremely easy grader, but the instructions are very unclear and confusing. Doesn't really teach. But honestly, as long as u put in a little bit of effort on the assignments, you'll get an A.

Easy class, but Prof. Doyle teaches very fast and not always clearly, so would not recommend him if you aren't able to teach yourself the programs. Very nice, typically let out class early. Cares about his students and wants them to learn. Doesn't give an exact rubric, but follow the instructions and what he says in class and you will succeed.

Professor Doyle is very approachable and knows his material very well! Be sure to pay attention in class and put time into doing your work well — the quality of your work will clearly show in your grade. Some of the material (especially HTML) is hard, but Professor Doyle is happy to give you help if you need it. Take MEJO-121 with him!

Professor Doyle is the kindest guy ever! There were points where it felt like we had a lot of projects due at once, but he gives them out far in advance. He's very accessible and understanding of literally everything. This class really touches on every type of digital media and he gives great feedback without hurting your grade. Take his class!!

analysis.name: Pauline Blaimont
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Blaimont was pretty great. I genuinely enjoyed her lectures and was interested in the content even though I am not a Bio major. Just try not to miss any homework or quizzes because she won't let you make anything up unless you get hit by a car or something. Overall pretty epic teacher.

Dr. Blaimont was amazing! This class had a lot of content and work, but her lectures and teaching style always prepared me. Her exams were difficult in the right ways, testing things in an understandable manner from lectures and work. 220 had a lot of content, but I feel like she made it as manageable as possible. Take her if you have the chance!

Dr. Blaimont was probably the best 220 professor ever. I was so terrified for this class and she was the nicest person ever. Her lectures were clear and engaging, and didn't mind explaining something slowly in class when I asked for help. Office hours are great, exams are fair, and she is hilarious! Don't miss the chance to take a class with her!

Blaimont is an amazing professor. She is very kind, very enthusiastic about the subject (she is young and relatively new), and very straightforward about what she wants from her students. She is also very accessible outside of class for questions, help, and anything else. 100% the best option to take for 220!

God-tier of a professor. Definitely take Dr. Blaimont for BIOL 220! Very fair exams and grading on assignments. Patient on answering questions. I wish she would answer questions more directly, but she is already doing an amazing job for her 1st semester at UNC! Study the ppt and journal club, then you will be fine!

analysis.name: Meredith Petschauer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Although the professor is kind, the exams are very challenging and account for 80% of the final grade. The PowerPoints are bland, making it difficult to learn the material without rewriting and reviewing notes outside of class. Homework is graded very specifically. Challenging for students without a physics background.

I came into this class not having any physics background so I was super nervous, but both Dr. P & the ULAs were super helpful in office hours & class. Dr. P always made lectures relatable and super interesting. She does tend to overcomplicate concepts at times, so I recommend going to ULA office hours to uncomplicate things. I loved this class!

I enjoyed having Petschauer as a prof, shes hilarious and makes lecture less boring. The material for this class was very hard and I found it very difficult to study for the exams. Office hours were key but almost every exam, I felt like I was going into it blind. most of the class relies on exam and there was 1 or 2 quizzes & easy group project.

Unapproachable professor. Had to teach myself everything. Textbook homeworks + in-class quizzes you can't make up + 4 exams + 1 (easy) project. Always misgraded exams & hw. Would recommend taking pass/fail if you're not a physics buff.

She is a great professor, while the material is hard, she did a great job communicating how to work through the problems. The first exam was a bit of a shock though as to how much was conceptual over mathematical.

analysis.name: Yue Qiu
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Qiu does not explain concepts in class: he reads straight from the PowerPoints. He doesn't even try, even if students ask him to write out explanations in class. Stay away, if possible. I do not know why he is teaching intro physics as he does not seem to care whatsoever.

This is actually for Phys 115. I cannot hear Qiu, he just reads off the slides and WHISPERS. He doesnt explain anything or write anything to solve it he just talks. Please avoid him, you will not learn.

Professor Qiu struggled to read the slideshows, which made understanding difficult physics topics even harder. In fact, I got a better grade in 118 than 114 just because of how bad professor Qiu was. He also never answers questions, always seems nervous to lecture, and seems so out of touch with his students. if you have a class with him, DROP IT.

Just don't. It's clear he's very nervous up there and I feel bad for the guy, but you literally can't hear a word of what he says. And I sit near the front of the lecture hall. He's someone who may be too smart for his own good. It's much more productive to watch the YouTube lectures from 2020 during class and follow along with poll everywhere.

He needs to take a public speaking seminar before teaching again. Also he needs better awareness instead of staring down, as I saw a girl with her hand up for over 3 minutes without him so much as looking at her.

analysis.name: Qing Gong
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Gong was a great professor because she actually put effort into teaching rather than the flipped classroom style of some other econ classes. Problems challenged us and really tested our understanding of the material without being "trick questions." I loved this class and thought it was relevant to contemporary policy problems.

Dr. Gong is one of the best econ professors I've had. You can clearly tell that she is passionate about the subject, and mentions real life applications. If you're confused on anything, Dr. Gong will clarify everything during office hours. The class isn't as easy as some claim, and you do have to put in effort.

I LOVED her. She doesn't try to trick you at all and gives you everything you need to succeed. Exams are extremely similar to problem sets and hw. She is always there to help if anything is needed and such a nice person. Can't speak highly enough about her!! 100% take this as an Econ elective.

Dr. Gong is a really great professor and lenient grader. She really wants you to do well which is uncommon in UNC Econ. Best professor I have had in UNC Econ not because I did well but she is so passionate about teaching. This is good to see and something that UNC Econ needs more of.

Professor Gong was one of the kindest professors I have ever had. She is very accessible outside of class and she genuinely wants to help you succeed. The class consists of short homework assignments and one group project that you work on throughout the semester. I cannot recommend this class and Professor Gong enough. Take this class if you can!!

analysis.name: Roberto Quercia
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I enrolled in PLAN363 for a free A, and I wish I hadn't abused this class as much as I did (attendance-wise). He is genuinely so kind and clearly cares about what he is presenting. Please make sure to go to his classes, he teaches very valuable information that I wish I didn't take for granted. Highly recommend!

He is very unclear in his lectures about the topics that we actually need to know. Also..what a snooze fest., and he doesn't know how to work technology AT ALL. If you want the class for somewhat easy credit then sure, take the class, but don't expect to come out of it knowing anything useful about personal finance that you can't find online.
Very easy class if you want an A, The lectures can get a tad boring but again, it's easy and you could get an A just zoning out in lectures and reading the slides later.

TA's did majority of grading and gave good feedback, class was not hard at all, although the lectures could be boring at times.  Quizzes came straight from the slides as well as the final, which was online.  Pretty useful class and information.  Final questions were pulled from quizzes

Very easy class, good easy A. There is a financial plan that TAs grade, my year the TA's were very nice. There are 2 "true/false" questions every class to make sure you're present. Those were kind of annoying but you can find the answer pretty easily. The quizzes were 10 questions (there were 3) those were also pretty easy. Final was online.

analysis.name: Qi Zhang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is a sweet person who cares about students and someone who likes to see you truly understand and learn from class content. This is the most diverse class I have every took with people coming from all kinds of backgrounds and ages. 10/10 would recommend!

Dr. Qi is an amazing professor, who offers great and enjoyable experience to students in class. He does excellent jobs to help students understand the concepts and develop programming skills with hands-on exercises. He is ready to give feedback and cares about your performance. I would definitely take his other classes if any.

I absolutely loved Prof. Zhang! He is such a nice, caring, and considerate guy. Definitely one of the best professors I had at UNC, and I will for sure take his class again. He gives really good lectures. Do not hesitate to take his class, it's an easy A, I promise.

I enjoyed this class & Qi's teaching; it was one of my top 3 at UNC. He often gave extensions and was great with partial credit for late work. There were times in class where he didn't give us answers, but after he hinted that the question was on the midterm! Attendance & group work are important, but I'd def take another class with Qi

Taking Geog 567 with Dr Qi was a honor. I left this class with more knowledge, super cool projects, and the desire to learn more. Dr Qi went out of his way to make sure I was learning and understanding the material. He would encourage me and I never felt stupid. I wish I could take all my classes with him.

analysis.name: Qi Sun
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The worst math professor I've had. His lectures are extremely difficult to understand and follow. It's much easier to understand the course by just reading the textbook, but since he does some proofs in lecture only and won't publish those notes, you still have to go to class. He did not curve any midterms despite a plurality of students failing.

I took MATH566 with him. HARDEST B- OF MY LIFE. I did all the homework, read through the textbook multiple times, and took great notes, and still ended up with a 70 avg on the midterms (he doesn't curve btw). I missed ONE CLASS the whole semester, and missed one proof (not in the textbook) that he then made 20% of a whole exam grade. DO NOT TAKE

The worst professor I have ever had. In addition to everything else that has been said, he simply doesn't care about teaching. I went to his OH 30 minutes before they ended, and right after I knocked on his door, he proceeded to pack up his things and leave while ignoring me. Impossible to reach over email. Didn't curve midterms. Don't take!

Not a great lecturer, hard to understand and kinda just teaches from the textbook but these reviews are unnecessarily harsh. Sun is a bro. Nice guy, pretty chill dude, helps students as much as he can while preserving reasonable course standards. Small quizzes instead of HW, easy exams with no trick questions (usually just copies of book problems).

The worst professor I have ever had at UNC. Exams were strictly based on textbook proofs, homework questions, or proofs in lecture. Lecture notes not given and textbook gave computational algorithms while our exams were by hand. Mostly a kind person to talk to but can be rather condescending when trying to learn and ask questions. Never take.

analysis.name: Wei Quan

The pressure to publish papers and secure funding often overshadows commitment to delivering engaging and high-quality lessons.  Adopt a dismissive or authoritarian attitude towards students, which discourages open dialogue and critical thinking in the classroom.
Wei needs to improve his  expression skills, probably because his mother tongue is not English, and sometimes I can't fully understand what Wei wants to express in class.

I took the German summer course online, and unfortunately, I found the experience quite frustrating. While I understand the challenges of teaching virtually, I felt that the instructor was not well-prepared for the online format. The instructions were often unclear, and communication lacked consistency.
Won't recommend this course for beginners
Very bad attitude and arrogant

analysis.name: Quoc Tran-Dinh

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Tran-Dinh, in both his first year of teaching and first year in the country, graded strictly, and rapport with students was nonexistent. He seems like a very nice man, but lectures were confusing, and office hours confused concepts further. Definitely the hardest professor for STOR 113. Hopefully his teaching will improve with experience.
Class itself is very boring, but he gives extra credit opportunities and curves a lot

415 is a very boring class compared to others in the statistics major. Quoc is an okay professor, but implements strange curves and refuses to give back points when his TAs make grading mistakes. Lots of tedious homework that isn't always relevant to what is tested. But overall, relatively fair class

Professor Quoc treats being a professor like a second job. He does an extremely bad job at teaching the concepts in class which leads to a lot of extra time spent learning the same concepts that were taught in class. There are always typos in the in-class quizzes and practice questions which leads to wrong answers and unsolvable problems.

Quoc taught a new course and, considering the difficulty in balancing a new course, did a great job designing it. He adjusted the pace of the course when he realized we were struggling and provided sufficient feedback on assignments. The tests and quizzes were very difficult, but he curved appropriately. Reasonably understanding if you reach out.

analysis.name: Andreas Quist
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Prof Quist is pretty chill for M130 He knows his stuff but sometimes he speeds through it. If you don't get smth,hit him up during office hours.He gives good feedback if you actually ask for it. His lectures can get kinda dry, like my skin (i have eczema), but if you stay focused, you'll be good. Hes a prof who cares & knows what he's talking about

Professor Andreas isn't the best professor for math 130. He does have very good "teaching" skills and doesn't know how to explain the content well. However if you are able to go to office hours and have one on one time he does go into more depth about a concept. To do well on the exams just go over study guides prior to. He repeats questions.

Andreas is not a very good teacher. He goes through the information way too fast. He shows it and does not explain methods. If you ask a question during lecture you will end up more confused. Andreas also missed and canceled many lectures in the middle of fall. Our class asked for him to postpone the test or review more and he said no.

He missed a lot of classes during the middle of the semester which made it really hard to understand the material and do well. The tests are very hard but he gives a ton of partial credit. He is never available outside of class and doesn't respond to emails, ever, no matter what. I would definitely take another teacher for the course.

Professor Quist wasn't a great teacher; he would miss classes and he was new to teaching so most lectures were confusing. I didn't even really pay attention during lectures, I just did the pre-class work and studied well before the exams. But he did offer extra credit on tests and made good study guides for the exams.

analysis.name: Brenda Quinones-Ayala
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Quinones-Ayala was an absolute joy to have as a professor. So caring, enthusiastic, and engaging with her students. Spanish 203 is a hard class, but she was very encouraging if you ever made mistakes and would explain them in a very understandable way. Some of her grading took a long time but I can't even care because of how amazing she was.

Funny and bubbly- Brenda is my favorite out of all instructors I've had thus far at UNC.  She's caring, passionate, personable, and truly understands the Spanish language (as she is a native Puerto Rican.)   I went to office hours for help on a paper & she not only worked through my paper with me, but also asked about my interests and future plans.

Dr. QA was extremely kind, caring, enthusiastic, understanding, and accommodating. I am not the best Spanish speaker but was able to get through this class because I made an effort. If you care, you will do fine because she cares! A great option (if not one of the best) for 203.

Genuinely one of the best professors I have encountered during my time at UNC. Take her class if you can, while SPAN203 can be difficult, she will do anything to support you and make learning Spanish fun and accessible.

Professor Quinones-Ayala was my favorite spanish teacher of all time! She was hilarious and generally cared about her students. I felt seen and competent, even when I completely messed stuff up as is bound to happen in a language class. She did the absolute best she possibly could with the freedom she was given, and I am so grateful.

analysis.name: Ross White
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. White was a difficult professor, but if you are serious about poetry, he makes your writing GOOD, really makes you think more broadly than you might have coming out of an intro/intermediate classes. He is almost clairvoyant when he prescribes you individual readings, and he will make your poetry better with his challenges.

ENGL 259 is an improvisation class that fulfills my GE requirement and the screenwriting track. The class is fun and low-pressure. We practice improv in class and write weekly journals. There is no midterm or final. We have two formal theatre performances, and you can learn a lot from performing in public and developing comedy-writing skills.

He's so caring about us as people and our growth. Accessible outside class. He will push you HARD but it's worth it. Be ready for a lot of work, but know it's not pointless and all very thoughtfully designed. Great guy willing to go to bat for anyone, and well respected

Prof White takes your work very seriously and expects that you will too, but if you work with him your writing WILL improve a great deal. This class was a LOT of work but it hardly felt like work, it was all edifying and will stretch you in the best way. If you're willing to put in the effort to learn and grow, Prof White is a fabulous instructor.

The workload is hefty, but it never feels like busywork. Prof White makes it clear that he cares about you as an individual and your personal artistic growth. His feedback is sooo helpful (def go to his office hours!) and he has definitely helped me to become a better poet! I would 1000% take a class with him again, and you should too!

analysis.name: Richard Smith
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is very friendly and the class can be dry but is straightforward. Gives very helpful practice materials for midterms. Very accommodating on deadlines and changed the class based on our math backgrounds. Daily quiz for attendance. 1 HW each week that takes < 2hours

Probably one of the best options for the required 500 level class in the statistics major. Exams are all open book/open note and align very well with practice exams. Difficult but reasonable given the course level. Homework takes about 2-3 hours per week.

Dr. Smith tries to enable students to understand the intrinsically difficult material for the Advanced Methods of Data Analysis class. Since this class is both heavily theoretical and applicational, the class is hard to teach by nature. But Dr. Smith did really well communicating the content. Tests are fair but require attention to detail.

Professor smith has been one of the best professors I've had at Carolina. He cares about his students and helps his students succeed. He gives extra credit and can be lenient on the exams when needed. One homework per week and class can be long and boring but in my opinion it is one of the easiest statistics classes. I would recommend taking him.

Grade comes mostly from tests. Prof Smith is obviously very knowledgable about the subject. Lectures can be pretty boring though. Tests involved many questions in a little too short of a time so you had to rush during the two midterms. Not too hard to get a good grade if you take good notes though.

analysis.name: Cdc Reeve
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, THE BEST professors I've had here.  If you don't like reading or are closed minded you probably won't enjoy the class.  If you are willing to challenge yourself some then you will GAIN SO MUCH.  I could sit and listen to him lecture all day. Don't go into the class looking for a grade, look for an experience and the grade will come.

Great at simply laying out major problems. Enjoyable lectures that were well delivered. Many mostly well-chosen assigned readings in this course. I am sure his other classes are more difficult--PHIL 112 (sometimes taught by others) is an introductory/overview course. He knows his Greek! And he can rattle off extensive quotes from various texts!

Reeve is a great, clear professor who really knows what he's talking about. He is pretty intimidating though, so if you don't have a good TA, your questions may not get answered. He very clearly outlines the readings so you don't really have to read the books, but the exams are not easy at all, unless you're pretty good at philosophy already.

Reeve is a joy to listen to and he really knows his stuff (and is quite aware that he knows it). Readings can generally be skipped if you attend lecture, but they can help to understand the material. This class can be a challenge if you don't think the way Reeve does, but if you do you're golden

Reeve is quite possibly one of the most intelligent men alive. He is just bursting with information. He doesn't really care if you speak or not because he loves to be able to just share what he thinks and why. Do your readings, it'll help immensely. He only gives 2 grades a semester & no exams, so you'll need to do well but he wont let you fail.

analysis.name: Donald Reid
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 70 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Donald Reid is a very smart guy, but has trouble getting his points across. He will pose very dynamic questions at the beginning of class and seldom arrive on an answer. The T.A.'s are your best resource. They will explain anything that you are confused about because they understand how jumbled Prof. Reid's lectures really are.

If I have one piece of advice, take HIST398 with Dr. Reid. He's so awesome at giving feedback, always checking in on us as people, built good community in class, and easy to reach outside of class. He made the paper feel less daunting. 1000/10 recommend one of my favorite professors at UNC!!!!!

The lectures aren't very engaging and you really have to pay attention to what he is saying because not all the material is on the slides. That being said, there aren't too many assignments. As long as you read the assigned material and participate in recitation you will be fine. It does mainly depend on the TA that you get and how hard they grade.

Professor Reid is very kind and encouraging. Although the class has a lot of reading (80-100 pages of reading due per class), I found the material fascinating. Classes are almost all discussion, so participation matters!

Lectures aren't too engaging, but some content (eg Israel/Palestine, the environment, Apartheid) is very relevant, & the readings/films are interesting. You need to love history to enjoy the class, though, and 3-page essay limits can make it tough to say everything I want to (one required us to use 4 sources!). Worthwhile class for some but not all

analysis.name: Christopher Shepard

He will start class by talking about his dogs, and we are always behind in lecture. We typically talk about material from a day or two before. You'd be better off taking 101 with another professor.

Chem 101 is notoriously difficult but standardized, so it has nothing to do with the professor. Dr. Shepard is super kind and always encourages class participation. He's a great teacher and seems like he genuinely cares about students and ULs. Love hearing his dog stories and analogies!
Only went to his GPSS sessions and he's great. Doesn't make you feel bad for not understanding the content

analysis.name: Sarah Shields

review_highlights.comment: Professor Shields is extremely knowledgeable when it comes to Middle Eastern studies. She's also very approachable so take advantage of the paid lunches she offers. Yes, you have to put some effort but its worth it.

bad experience. Shields lectures only 20% of the time the rest are guest lectures, creating inconsistency in style and structure. Accent/lang barriers and frequent shifts make content hard to follow. Shields often misspeaks, and heavy Perusall/readings create an overwhelming, misaligned workload. 3 books to buy on top of that

Professor Shields is really great. Lectures are interesting and there are often guest speakers. Most of your grade is dependent on a semester-long project. A nitpicky TA graded the first couple of things, but the other grades were pretty easy (including the final paper). Having to read a lot for every class is a bit annoying, but it's manageable.

I wish she was a bit more organized with the topics she taught. She was a kind woman regardless; I did feel a bit dismissed at times in class, but she was always very kind. She tried to teach political matters in a historical sense, which was a bit weird, kind of nonethelss though.

I was very disappointed in this class. The lectures were confusing & disjointed, the powerpoints useless, and the essays extremely frustrating bc of the former two. I took this class to get a general basis of knowledge in the Middle East, and that failed miserably. I only recommend this course if you are already well-versed in the region.

analysis.name: Conghe Song

The tests would occasionally include questions on super minor details, but other than that were pretty easy to do well on, especially if you go to class regularly.  Very few assignments outside of tests.  A super nice guy and a 10/10 course!

Dr. Song is one of the best professors I have ever had! 410 focused on using MatLab to model the environment. He taught the program from scratch and was great at it. The labs were really cool and fairly straightforward. Also, he is very accessible outside of class!

The class wasn't too difficult, but the assignments often felt surface level to me, and group projects were a big part of the grade. I didn't love the lectures, which often felt dry. However, Professor Song was caring and went out of his way to help students succeed.

He's a really nice guy who will try to help you out. He puts a lot on his website, but to do well in the class, you really have to go unless you enjoy the material. Very nice professor who is a good teacher and wants all his students to succeed.

May be the smartest person you will have the pleasure of listening to. Is an incredibly capable quantitative scientist. If you are interested in remote sensing and ecosystem modeling you will learn TONS from this class. Highly Recommended!

Amazing professor. If you're struggling in this class, it's not on him it's on you. He's tough, blunt, and expects you to act like an adult. People who complain are just soft and not ready for real expectations. If you can "handle" honesty and want to actually learn, take his class. Highly recommend.

I read the comments and had some apprehension coming into the class. I was amazed about how the comments were totally wrong. I'm a Jr and many of the ppl were Sr. who were complaining. Super student‑focused. He invited feedback throughout the term and actually used it. His real‑world examples helped the material stick, and he made sure everyone participated. Would definitely take his class again. To stay in the loop, you must come to class.

analysis.name: Uffe Bergeton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Dr Bergeton clearly cares a lot about the content but his lectures were not very captivating as someone who didn't already have a passion for the topic. I did enjoy the freedom in the final paper which allowed me to dive into really any aspect of Qin and Han history/culture. If you already know you love the topic, you'll enjoy this more than I did.

He definitely knows what he's talking about, but is terrible at teaching a simplified version of it. He goes off on really long unrelated tangents and is generally confusing. Definitely go to office hours because he is picky. Not to mention, he is white but claims to be "Chinese" as a result of marrying a Chinese woman.

There are quite a lot of readings, but they all relate in a way and most of the readings are online. 2 essays, one being the midterm, and the final being a 10pg paper along with a 5 min presentation. He is a very generous grader and the lectures were pretty interesting. He holds office hours for essay critique so you can score better on the essays.
hard course but he is a nice guy.the materials are hard though, i don't know the stories in the slides even though I'm a Chinese
uffe is so nice in class and is really gentle during lectures, but the grading is absolutely horrible. TA also grades really irresponsibly.

analysis.name: Robert McDonough

review_highlights.comment: You could know every concept in depth and study profusely and still struggle with the exams, which make up 70% of your grade. I have never gotten anything below an A in my life and I near failed some of his tests. Lectures were interesting and I learned a lot. Tests on concepts we never practiced. Sent me straight to my therapist twice. Don't take.

The one takeaway I have for this course is to lower my expectations before checking canvas. He prides himself on class averages being below 60%. The only things this class has taught me are to humble myself and that i'll never be prepared enough for his exams. This class is unnecessarily hard and he refuses to acknowledge it. King of gaslighting.

Robert is honestly one of the worst professors I've had here. The exams are virtually impossible and he likes his averages to be in the 60s. He makes TONS of mistakes on exams which causes grading to be delayed and overall confusion. You might as well guess on the short answers because he never explains how to do them. Good luck if you have him.

It's as bad as they say. McDonough's exams are impossible. I can't count how many times we have been interrupted mid-exam because of multiple errors and typos on them. Spends more time worrying about cheating than teaching the material or checking his exams for errors, which are 70% of your grade, and the average is a 66%. Avoid at ALL COSTS.

Professor McDonough is very enthusiastic about the material but his exams are unnecessarily complicated. I found the multiple choice sections to be a joke, while the short answers were very difficult solely due to poor wording rather than students lack of understanding of the material. Also, he just pisses me off sometimes.

analysis.name: Elaine Townsend Utin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: AMAZING! Elaine is a true gem and I would HIGHLY recommend anyone to take her class. It is full of so much helpful and important information and she has passion behind everything she does. She is also super compassionate, and understanding of the chaos that was 2020. She held plenty of spaces for healing and for growth in combination with learning.

As an Education Professor Elaine really knows how to effectively foster a nurturing learning environment where everybody feels heard and respected. She is sweet and fun and lights up every class with her bright attitude and passion for what she teaches. She may honestly be too good for the classes she teaches. She takes radical pedagogy seriously.

Profe is amazing and a true gem at UNC. Her class is so interesting and a must take for any Latine person at UNC. It is a great class to explore your own identity and understand the world around you. Profe creates a safe space for people to be vulnerable and honest about their experiences. You really begin to feel at home in class.

analysis.name: Beril Ulku-Steiner
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Had a phony and fake nice personality in lecture but if you approached her one on one, she was inflexible both in her availability and in her willingness to help outside of class. She assigns an case study paper with vague and unclear parameters and expectations, and she has questions on the test from videos we watched in class weeks earlier. SUCK!

Dr. U-S will come to class every day cheery and smiley but DONT LET IT FOOL YOU. It is mandatory to go to class even though the way you will learn the material is purely through reading - she does not help. She will assign a group project and about 11 pg paper but don't count on a good grade, she'll rip you on both no doubt. Tests are ok if you stu

She smiles a lot; don't let it fool you.  Instructions for things are completely unclear.  EXTREMELY harsh grader, tests on things that we never talked about in class.  Scope of information way too large.  Extremely picky.  She was late to every meeting I had with her (meetings that she required), didn't show up, or just postponed them last minute.

Although she was a bubbly professor at 8 AM, I learned very quickly that turns into a very condescending demeanor. She grades incredibly tough and does not give good feedback. It's really disappointing considering how much I was looking forward to this class. The lectures were mandatory but not helpful, pretty much taught myself all the material.

If you can avoid taking Professor US for Abnormal Psyc (or any class), then PLEASE DO. Horrible professor. Ridiculous grader. The group project and accompanying paper was a complete joke, as she graded unfairly, extremely harsh and her rubric was unclear. Don't let the happy demeanor fool you. Also, 1 unexcused abstence failing attendance grade.

analysis.name: James Umbanhowar
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Terrible.  Not even worth going to class.  I started reading the book before the class lectures and I started to think I could have taught the class better than he did.  He stutters a lot and spends the vast majority of the time talking about simple concepts and completely avoids the nitty-gritty details.  I also hated his voice.
Absolutely terrible.  Lectures made 0 sense. The recitations are the only thing that  saved me from failing

It is true that his lectures are a little vague and he speaks really fast but there is a lot information that he has to cover in a small amount of time. He tries his best to be helpful and make the class interesting and overall is not a bad professor. The class is tough but the exams are not impossible and the curve is usually pretty good.

Umbanhowar's lectures are worthless. He stands up there and discusses vague examples and graphs, and doesn't have a clear point. It's better to just read the textbook to understand the material. The tests aren't too hard and are curved ALOT because everyone does poorly. I would stay away from him and his poor ecology teachings.

You definitely need to have a good understanding of stats to take this class (and understand it). You can get by with all of the assignments by going to office hours and simply doing the assignments (those are 80% of the grade and no exams), but you won't really understand it without a baseline understanding of stats.

analysis.name: Peter Uhlenberg
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Overall his class is very enjoyable, he makes the class very interesting. Although the class might seem very easy watch out! His exams are very detailed you have to really know it all. A lot of reading, in the book and articles he assigns. Overall I liked him

analysis.name: Melissa Venegas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Profesora Venegas was a great professor! She's super caring and made classes enjoyable. The SPAN 261 curriculum (at least when I took it in fall 2024) was standardized between all of the professors, so I can't really say anything about the course itself that applies to just her. I'd definitely take a class with her again though!

She is the most caring and understanding teacher I have ever had! There's homework for most class days but it doesn't take long at all. One midterm and one final exam and a project. I would highly recommend taking span 267 with her. She is not a harsh grader at all and gives helpful feedback.

She seems nice, but I was having a tough time understanding the concepts, and when I approached her during office hours, she refused to help. She also grades very strictly and gives few and unhelpful comments. The class as a whole is set up awfully, but that's the department's fault.

Professor Venegas clearly cared about the content shown in class in context to our heritages as students. She is super bubbly and provides a comfortable environment to discuss perspectives on the material provided. Gonna miss her and mis compañeros!

Professora Venegas is a wonderful lecturer and a great Spanish teacher!! She is very sweet and understanding so never hesitate to go and talk to her. Her grading is also pretty chill and she will help you as much as she can. There's a lot of in-class participation and quite a few quizzes but just pay attention to deadlines and you'll be good.

analysis.name: Victoria Le-Sweatman
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Attendance is very important, and you have to participate and talk each recitation. Her feedback for assignments is very vague but it is clear she is looking for something very specific which she does not always tell you. Once you understand what she wants the recitations are easier, but she doesn't make this very easily known.

Recitation instructor. RMP reviews had me worried, but she was a fair grader with exams and weekly participation (80% for showing up, full points for speaking at least once). She also created a great classroom environment by leading discussions on sensitive topics.

This is for COMM 450. She will give you grades well below what you should have gotten. She has no rubrics and incredibly vague guidelines for assignments. She will give little tangible feedback and the difference between getting an 85 or 78 is completely unknown. If it is possible, avoid this professor.

I took this course online, and to be as tough as a grader that she is, she gives ZERO feedback. I technically ended with an 87, but thankfully the final grade was curved. These assignments were dreadful and so unrewarding to get no help or feedback. I would not have done well on my final essay if it weren't for her not being the one to grade it.

This class was not the worst class ever, but the rubrics for the speeches can be a little unclear. Along with this, her office hours aren't always entirely helpful because she does not give specific feedback that goes from your speech specifically. Overall, not a bad class. I also never read the textbook ever even though it was required.

analysis.name: Pablo Vega

Professor Vega is extremely knowledgable. can't really teach. I could have learned so much from him except that we barely got through any material. Cancelled class all the time, didn't grade anything till the last week, but did give feedback on assignments.
Pablo is absolutely the best professor! Super awesome and so gifted!

Pablo was super nice and the class work was not super hard. There was an online quiz that i missed as I had work and it brought my grade down to a B- from and A. I was not allowed to take it with a penalty or anything, just lost the points. This was frustrating as the class was not supposed to hurt my gpa and inevitably did.

analysis.name: Krysten Voelkner
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Krysten was awesome. Her class is environmentally focused, which is not usually something I would enjoy focusing on, but she ran it so well that I ended up liking it a lot. She encourages discussions/debate in class (especially materialism vs. idealism). If you are a reasonably strong writer, you will have zero issues and appreciate the discussions

Krysten is such a unique and interesting professor to have. She really just cares about you becoming a better writer, without making you jump through hoops. She is very clear on what she is looking for and will let you resubmit papers for a regrade if you are not happy. I think most people in this class will end with an A.

She was great, very approachable, an excellent choice for ENGL105. The class will be environmentally focused, even if you're taking a specific concentration of the class like humanities. I found her grading to be very lenient, everything I turned in was an easy A.

She is great. She's super down-to-earth, gives no tests, and pretty much grades all projections/essays on completion(I ended with a 100.0), as long as you put effort and follow her instructions. She focuses a lot on plants from various perspectives to teach class, so if you find that boring, she may not be for you, but definitely extremely easy A.
Her Engl105 is focused around environmental studies, which usually bores me to death, but she kept things interesting. If you're a competent writer you'll be absolutely find with her.

analysis.name: Vladas Pipiras

analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Professor Pipiras was great. Although teaching seems very fast paced content coverage was excellent.
If you do put time in you will definitely get an A . Extremely easy tests and if the entire class is not doing good in it he reduces 0.5 points instead of 1 point for every wrong question. Very easy going grader .
Recommended for everyone.

Professor Pipiras is excellent and easy to communicate with! Sets clear grading criteria, has well-prepared documents, and gives moderately hard midterms. STOR 120 is not a very challenging class and you get what you pay for.

If you're thinking of taking STOR 120 over STOR 155, I would take 155 instead if you have little to no coding experience. Weekly labs and homeworks take about 2-3 hrs each. His lectures consist of him doing the code and you copying it down but fairly quick. He is a nice guy but overall goes quickly and lots of homework.
Professor Pipiras is very kind and understanding. He uploads a lot of useful material on Canvas for students to use. The class is well-planned.

This is a good class. It is a little difficult for those without much coding experience. However, the professor makes it easy to learn and as long as you are being diligent and learning, it's great. Grading is pretty chill and a lot of boosts come in later on. Prof. Pipiras is decently lenient on grading tests which helps a lot.

analysis.name: Maharshi Vyas

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Vyas is a really cool guy overall. His lectures are interesting and it's clear that he is very knowledgable about the subjects. I took this class for an FC and it actually expanded my POV on a subject I wouldn't have otherwise studies. Prof. Vyas is great and this class is not stressful, a nice break from harder classes. 100% take again.

He is one of my favorite professors I've ever had! He's a super kind person and very clearly extremely knowledgeable on what he is teaching, and passionate about it. However, he still gives students ample time to discuss topics on their own, which is probably my favorite aspect of the class. His class Reli 388  isn't very work heavy either!

Honestly an amazing professor. One in class test that is graded well and showcases what one truly took from the class material. He is extremely accessible outside of class and so caring. Truly knows the content and welcomes differing ideas and opinions. I recommend taking his course(s) and if I can, I will again.

M. Vyas is a great professor! Super engaging during office hours and cares about his students ability to succeed. Had a small class cohort this semester but he's looking for new students to join and I would def encourage you to do so! His RELI 388 class has FC Global/Ethics and there's only one SHORT midterm exam. The rest is fun projects, etc.

If you are interested in learning more about Hinduism and Hindus as a diaspora I recommend RELI 281. We learned many interesting things about their history/religion/culture and how communities adapt to new settings. Prof. Maharshi is very nice, a fair grader, and all you need to do is read the material and participate to earn a good grade.

analysis.name: Vicki Chanon
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I would love to say this is an awful class to get off her waitlists lol, but Dr. Chanon is an amazing professor. She's incredibly kind and personable and learns everyone's name, and her lectures are fun to attend. This class was mainly group project focused with that taking the place of the final, which I really enjoyed. 20/10 reccomend Dr. Chanon.

I love Vicki down! Super kind and cracked me up all semester. She learns everyone's names and her in-class participation is engaging and solidifies concepts. Exams are pretty straightforward, 2 homework drops, and quizzes that you can take until you get a 100. You can also miss 6 classes which is nice. Very easy class and an excellent prof.

One of my favorite professors I've had at UNC! Her lectures are very engaging including fun activities to understand the content. Her exams are very straightforward and she also offers a few extra credit opportunities. Also, one exam is dropped, and you can take the quizzes as many times as you want. I genuinely enjoyed going to her class :)

I lOVE Dr. Chanon. The material in the class was somewhat hard to understand at first but I always understood it after she lectured on it. As long as you read most of the assigned textbook readings and pay attention, this class is super interesting and easy to do well in.

I absolutely adore Dr. Chanon! She's hilarious and gets to know every student in her class (and our lecture was definitely more than 50 people)! She's really great about posting slideshows and recordings! Number one tip is to fill out the outlines for learning checks! The lowest learning check is dropped! Homeworks are pretty easy too!

analysis.name: Patrick Vernon

Make sure to participate through talking in class or emailing him - he's interesting and truly cares a lot about VC.

PV is a really interesting guy who is very passionate about VC. His knowledge is a little outdated, and it's pretty clear that the VCs he brings in to talk to the class don't take him seriously, but love him anyway. Work is tedious, and your grade is dependent on who you pair up with for the projects. Heard this class is splitting into 2 classes.

Class is interesting if you choose an engaging start-up. I recommend double-checking with PV every single time you can because he will ALWAYS have his own "correct" way of looking at things. The work isn't hard... understanding what he expects is. Lectures are all over the place with long tangents. Asking him a question will lead to being interrupted by a response that goes in circles for 60 seconds without any helpful answer. HIGHLY recommend avoiding

Tries to organize a course around VCs but doesn't have experience in VCs. He is quite arrogant which hinders what is enjoyable in the course. He is simply an OK teacher not any real added value has been added after I took this course, I would rather read a book on VCs / Growth Equity myself and learn more without having to good through him...

analysis.name: Monica Lopez Vazquez

Loved Monica, can safely say that she can write me a recommendation letter in the future! She is so kind and made me happy to walk into her class every single day; I could not have made this first semester without her.

She made what could have been a boring grammar pre-req fun and she pushed us a lot. Definitely an amazing Spanish professor. Tests were tough but she gave us a huge extra credit at the end which helped a lot.

Very very nice and helpful. She genuinely cared about you and your grade and was accommodating. She was not intimidating and would help if you were struggling. Try to do most of the readings before each class though so you don't get lost.
Monica is a great Spanish teacher. She's super nice, open to questions, and helps you with mistakes instead of looking down on you for them. Make sure you come to class prepared though.

analysis.name: Danny Wu

Highly recommend INLS 382!

I learned a lot and really want to take time the amount of effort Professor Wu took to make sure his students learned the topics in the most meaningful way. Always went above and beyond and really a gem of the INLS department!

Danny is such a caring professor. The course is graded based on three short homework assignments and a multiple-choice final, for which he provides the correct answers beforehand so students can study.

analysis.name: Herica Valladares

review_highlights.comment: No required attendance in lecture unless you are worried about missing the notes. Had I known what this class would entail I never would have taken it. Your entire grade relies on two midterms and a final. Furthermore, Prof. V began to remove student's access to helpful study material (lecture videos) midway through the semester. Grading also takes a really long time, so I never really knew where I stood in the class.
Attendance isn't mandatory but such an easy class if you go. 6 participation in class writing assignments, a midterm, final, and a few essays. She's very understanding, highly recommend.

analysis.name: Xiangjia Kong

He was an okay professor for discrete, but sometimes seemed confused on what he was teaching or by simple questions students asked. A very tough grader and doesn't accept methods other than what was taught in class (even if its in the textbook/still correct). Office hours are slightly helpful for explanations.

Nice guy but harsh grader. He took off points easily by a few things, and homework were harshly graded. Final was not easy as agreed. It's hard to get decent grade in his class although he curved the boundary.
