HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

Professor Liu was great. I loved watching him get progressively covered in chalk throughout the lectures. 

Seriously though, Professor Liu is a great guy and his lectures cover enough content so reading the textbook is unnecessary. My only note is that there can sometimes be a slight language barrier when asking questions.

Professor Liu is very caring and understanding. I struggled a bit for the exams but if you show up to class, pay attention, and start studying early you'll be fine. 
His lectures are great and really clear, and you can tell he cares about the subject and the class. Great professor, choose him!

Dr. Liu is a GREAT prof. He rescheduled two exams to fit classes needs, includes extra credit, and has great lectures. He is hilarious, and very good at explaining concepts. Highly recommend taking. If you pay attention, you will get an A.

Xinyun is a good time! Never read the textbook and was able to get all necessary content from lecture which typically ended early for time to ask questions about HW (or eat lunch early lol). He's funny in class and cares a lot. I can't recommend him more.

analysis.name: Xinlin Ma

review_highlights.comment: She's just professional and cares about students. She made things more flexible for students even during a hard time. I got more feedback than I expected as a junior. I will say take her class again!

She's the nicest professor I've ever met at UNC! She hopes students can learn from the course and makes the course as easy as possible. The topic is interesting and we have lots of case study about different worldwide cities, such as Chicago, Beijing, etc. She is very reachable after class. I will definitely take her class again.

She was always available to help and had the best, most welcoming attitude. She tried to make learning the material fun and enjoyable, and I believe she succeeded. One of the best professors I have ever had. She cares so much about her students and her field.

She cared about her students and was very enthusiastic about teaching. Attendance was not taken and the class was graded by 7 short open-note quizzes, a presentation, two papers, and a final. All were very easy.
She's very kind and sweet, and always willing to help her students with anything.

analysis.name: Xingyu Cheng

His teaching got better over time, and he has office hours sections where he will sit and explain material to you. The first midterm was incredibly easy. The second midterm was a lot harder, but still chill if you study hard. Final is demonic, but he curves accordingly.

I left this class most days understanding the material! He starts with easier content and then builds on it so we have the foundation to understand harder concepts. Some proofs can be a little abstract, but lots of practice can help you be prepared for tests. His study guides were helpful but looking up other practices can be helpful.

Tiger is a really funny and patient professor! He is very approachable and wants all students to do well in his class, but sometimes his explanations were hard to follow. Reading the textbook is optional, but I would highly recommend reading it + doing the practice problems if you want to do well in the class!

Office hours and in-class questions were available and very helpful. The second midterm and final were more challenging than the first test, but he curved generously at the end. The textbook aligns well with the course material and is a useful reference

At the begining of this class he did not really know how to teach well, but as the class went on he got better. There are 3 exams, homework due usually every Wednesday and a final. On exam 2 and exam 3  we got opportunities for extra credit which are the harder exams that really helped my grade. If you pay attention to lectures you will be fine.

analysis.name: Yuqian Xu

The final was painful also she puts in grades extremely fast (same day we took the final) the final was really hard so just prep for that. I did not hence the grade (had an A all sem)

Yuqian is a great teacher and person, but I disagree with other reviews. Class is extremely test-heavy and the final was surprisingly difficult compared to other exams and course sections. Final dropped my final grade 3 thirds of a letter grade.

Dr. Xu truly cares about her students! She teaches at a very fast pace so we always get out of class early. She's very eager to answer questions and make sure students are successful. She also is open to helping students in non-class related things

Professor Xu is a fun and engaging professor. Her class covers all the content you need to know and I felt I had everything I needed to thrive. Class consists of problem sets, 2 midterms, a final, and a group project. the final was the hardest part of the class, but overall, I enjoyed this course and would take Professor Xu again.
Everything is extremely fair, give feedback real quick. I am not a math person, but I did better than I thought in this class. My favorite professor!

analysis.name: Molly Worthen

review_highlights.comment: Professor Worthen treats her students as if they are in middle school and makes it hard to succeed in her class with her various technology policies. Literally the worst class I have ever taken in my entire life. Stay far away from this course. The professors are extremely unorganized and just speak about nonsense the entire time.

Prof Worthen clearly cares about her field and talks about it passionately. My main critiques are the lack of rubrics, tough grading (which is mostly on TAs), and the way she sometimes speaks condescendingly. I wouldn't take a course with her again, but I did feel I learned from her. I appreciated that she gave multiple extra credit opportunities.

Professor Molly Worthen was the singular worst choice for a Freshman Triple-I professor. Her level as a professor is far above what any freshman who is not an intended history major should be able to match. Yet, she expects you to match her level if not exceed it. She constantly degrades and condicends her students and fellow professors.

Whatever you do, do not take this as your Triple-I requirement. It is the hardest one by far. Grading is very subjective based on who reads it, and your TA can purposely take off points without giving clear reasons why. I attended every single lecture ready to learn and studied profusely for each exam, and never got higher than a 90.

review_highlights.comment: Though Dr. Marin may seem strict, she is genuinely really nice! Her office hours were pretty helpful to go over exams or any content related questions!

Dont bother asking questions because she wont answer them. Pros - she's funny and sarcastic, really appeals to my sense of humor. My advice, dont take this class.

Dr. Bustamante-Marin is a GENIUS in the field and is very knowledgeable. She's the sweetest person if you take the time to actually talk to her. That said, she is a tough grader with exams with tricky wording (which she will not give points back on), and omg the lectures are so fast with sometimes 100s of slides. you learn a lot! DONT CRAM!!

I really like her as a person, she was very approachable and you can tell she knows what she is talking about. However, lectures were pretty uninspiring and the tests were horrendously written. Good news is about half of the questions on her exams are free points, but the others were often very ambiguous and did not focus on core concepts.

Her lectures are boring. They only go over a small part of the assigned readings, so you are basically teaching yourself. If you read the chapters you could skip the lectures. Exams are hard. Multiple select questions. For example, the choices would be A; B; C; A & B; or A , B, & C. Over half of the test consist of question in this format.

analysis.name: Xiaoming Liu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Xiaoming is a kind professor who is very passionate about what she teaches. She is slightly disorganized, and slow with grading, but she makes it relatively easy for students to succeed. She doesn't take attendance, and it's not necessary to come to every class.

Xiaoming as a person is a really nice lady but as a teacher, leaves much to be desired. Attendance isn't mandatory so only about 40% of the class shows up on a regular basis. I attended every class but didn't get much out of it. I wondered "why am I here?" The slides are boring and can be accessed online. Not a terrible class but needs improvement.

Xiaoming is extremely sweet and approachable. She understands that it is an intro level class that most people are taking for gen ed credit and even tells you that reading the textbook is not necessary. Her only grades are two midterms, the finals, and participation so it is essential you study for tests, but overall not a hard class.

Xiaoming is a sweetheart. She is really kind and you can tell she wants her students to understand and love geology the way that she does. With that being said, I found it difficult to pay attention in this class, for whatever reason. The material is not terribly difficult to understand, so take some notes and you should be fine.

Very structured and clear-cut class. Xiaoming is a wonderful person and she teaches the material very well. I'd highly recommend for students to take this class whether they are interested in geology or just trying to fulfill a Gen-Ed. Take caution though- you will have to study the lecture slides hard to get an A.

analysis.name: Bryan Yackulic
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had!! He is so incredibly kind, really cares about his students, and makes a point of getting to know you. If you have the option, TAKE IT WITH HIM!
Dr. Yackulic was great at keeping us in the loop with Honors Carolina events and resources and has some super interesting anecdotes of his own.

Professor Yackulic is amazing! He really cares for his students and gives great advice for freshman to use for their future college careers. Easy class, only five assignments total and a very easy final exam but class is pass or fail. Kayden Hunt is also an amazing TA!

Dr. Y is a walking W. He's interesting, funny, caring, & inspirational. HNRS 101 is EXTREMELY easy: it has 6 simple assignments total & is graded on a P/F basis. There are a lot of resources you get exposed to, and the material can really help orient yourself at UNC. Just attend class, do your small, easy assignments, and you're done!
This is a very easy pass/fail class and Dr. Yackulic is a very kind and understanding professor.

analysis.name: Xiangying Huang

Exams are multiple choice but extremely difficult to understand. Her lectures include maybe 1 or 2 examples while the rest is just her doing proofs that aren't helpful.

Goes through the material as if everyone in the class has already seen it and just needs a quick glance to understand the topics. Does complicated proofs in class; homework and exams are unrelated and difficult. Unless you have already taken STOR 435 and know all the material, this is a terrible professor to have to start learning it.

The final (40% of your grade) is a a MC test w/ no partial credit.

analysis.name: Jordan Young

Not work-heavy, but quiz-heavy with questions pulled from niche things she said like one time in class. She's a bit of a lazy professor but it was a chill class overall.

Thankfully it's not work heavy, but it's all about memorization of random stats for short quizzes, which is tough. Also it's week 13 and we haven't been given any information about the final project.

If you participate and she knows you, this class is a breeze. Not hard content, but some of my friends that never showed up were in danger of B's. lots of online (easy) quizzes, group project, final.

She was an amazing professor. She was very knowledgeable about the information, but also paired everything with detailed slides that would represent what was on the weekly quizzes. The quizzes were easy if you looked over the notes from the class before and she is very chill.

analysis.name: Yaron Shemer

Yaron is a great guy and is clearly passionate about the subject matter. Attendance is mandatory and participation is recommended since lectures are discussion based. Seeing a lot of negative reviews after the first midterm but she clearly realized it was too difficult and made the second midterm easier - class avg went from 65 to 80. 

a lot of homework but no final and shes a really generous grader. will give you full credit on the final project if you put a good faith effort in.

Very caring and funny guy, but wow this class is hard. Not a lot of materials besides lectures, textbook is not really used outside of recitations. If you prefer a more structured class, take MSA. analysis.name: Aaron Harcus

review_highlights.comment: Reads directly off slides, but somewhat interesting class if you're SUPER interested in music. Attendance was literally just a number given at the beginning of each class. Professor Harcus was a great lecturer, and I really learned a lot from this course! Class is fairly easy consisting of attendance, reading/listening responses, a listening exam, and final project which are all graded easily.

Professor Harcus truly cares about music so much, and he is so interested in all of his students' opinions on the music we all enjoy. He's super chill and very kind. I. Great man for a easy class, just show up to class and do the assignments as you are graded just for participation and short assignments. If you can't pass this class this easy, might be time to transfer out. Unbelievably easy trust me.

Professor Harcus is amazing, he is now one of my favorite Professor here at UNC! I would 100% take his class again! He is very understanding and the assignments were spaced out so it was very doable and I also enjoyed his lectures too!

analysis.name: Ron Bergquist

analysis.name: Aaron  Jacobson

analysis.name: Aaron Thieme

analysis.name: Aaron Smith

SUCH an amazing professor and even more awesome person. UNC comp sci does not deserve Aaron Smith. He makes everyone feel welcome, encourages questions, and is super understanding. I adore Aaron! So kind, very interactive lectures, really wants you to ask questions and learn, explains things so clearly - an overall 10/10. IMO he's right under Kris Jordan as best CS professors here. 301 is a great class because of him. He has so many fun catch phrases you could make a bingo.

April 19, 2021. 2:31 PM. Student: "We should make the PollEv answers 25% each." Overall, a great professor! I would say it was one of my best experiences in a class. analysis.name: Adam Price

Chill A, cool subject, if you're taking 130 take him

Adam was a super nice teacher and made the class feel very open for constructive criticism. My only complaint with him was his "Do Not" list for writing, but with the way he structured the class it never became an issue. He was flexible as well.

analysis.name: Adlai Lang
