He's the reason I decided to major in Public Policy. Best professor I've had yet. His lectures were very informational and hilarious. Great man.

He's the most respected professor in the Public Policy department, yet he teaches PLCY101, and does so extremely well. He makes lectures super laid back and funny, yet still informative. His top ten list is a gem, and he definitely cares about his students. Offers extra credit for going to forums! Overall, definitely a great professor.
Professor Gitterman is awesome! Such a cool dude and a fun class. Want to take something he teaches again.

One of the best professors I've had. Makes every class interesting and really cares about his students. It is well worth your time to come to class because he clarifies difficult points in the readings and makes the ideas from the textbook (READ IT TO SUCCEED IN CLASS!) more applicable. Wish I could take the class again or another course by him.

analysis.name: Denise Mitchell
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: boring lecture and attendance not required so you can get away with not going. tests were pretty easy as long as you complete the study guide. tests were mcq, true/false, fill in the blank, and frq. has review days before exam where you can earn extra credit for the midterm. overall p easy class

For the semester long project, everything is peer-reviewed until the final research brief meaning that it could fail to meet her standards when it's worth the largest portion of your grade. Extremely strict on grading for exams and provides no flexibility in answers. Lost an entire point out of 30 for using a synonym instead of the actual word.

Tests were horrible. She grades very strict and the questions are too broad. She gives barely any material to study and grades so specifically. Other than the tests the class is fine but the tests make it awful. You can skim the readings that are assigned every day. DO NOT RECOMMEND.

Horrible class, harsh grader, way too specific on her test for no reason, class was all done in lecture and a waste of time to go to, her in class assignments did nothing to reinforce the class content.

I enjoyed this class! She is very particular when it comes to grading exams, specifically the essay portions but as long as you complete the study guides you will do just fine in the class. Attendance is preferred but you can get by skipping if you need it. Easy A if you complete all the study guides!

analysis.name: Paul Delamater
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Dr. D is honestly one of my favorite GEOG professors! He explains concepts super well and actually seems to care and want to connect with his students. His class is pretty laid back and fun.

While there is nothing wrong with the course content, Delameter is very disrespectful and condescending in his feedback and when students ask questions. Never have felt scared to talk in a class before. For a class about technology, no question is a dumb question. Consider a student might be struggling with serious issues before you berate them.

Comes off as a pleasant and understanding person but your first conversation with him outside of class will make you change your mind immediately. He's so incredibly condescending and rude when you ask questions in office hours and doesn't actually care about helping you -- instead he just belittles. The TAs were the only redeemable part of him.

This was my first time really working with R, and Dr. D made it super approachable. Everything we did on a "major" grade assignment (hw or project) came straight from an in-class assignment or demo that we had access to. Very easy to do well if you take the time to pay attention to the coding. I thought the class was fun, and Dr. D is a good prof.

I love Dr. D and this class! I learned so much (you learn R) & he was really helpful with feedback & responding to emails & discussion posts. There's a semester-long final project, many coding assignments, demos, and in-class exercises. It's a lot but if you pay attention to his (sometimes boring) lectures and do everything on time you'll get an A.

analysis.name: JD Defreese
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Really nice prof. The lectures are really boring, but he really knows his stuff. Exams are trickier than you would think. Offers extra credit.

DeFreese's voice is the most monotone, boring voice ever. The content in this class is organized a little bit oddly and could be done better. It is just about a bunch of different theories you need to memorize. This class is one of worst classes I've taken at unc. Also, there is a big group project that is so busy work.

One of the worst classes I've taken at UNC. Probably the most boring professor. Focuses too much on useless group work when the room isn't even set up to work in groups. Makes the tests extra hard for no reason. This class is the reason I'm dropping the EXSS major

JD is a really good professor. He's very understanding and responds quickly to emails. He also grades really quickly. Our exam grades were released the afternoon after we took the test. Class can be challenging and instructions aren't always the clearest for the big group project. Exams are fair but not the easiest.

Professor Defreese is so kind and a great professor! He is a quick grader and gives you feedback to improve on future assignments. Class was group project heavy, but if you get a good group you are fine and he is not too harsh on the group papers or presentation. Tests straightforward. Groups made doing class assignments easier. Take him!

analysis.name: Janitor Derek

analysis.name: Diane Kelly

Worst class i have ever taken at UNC., This woman single-handedly made me hate Information Science. INLS 201 was a nitpicky, terrible and useless course, She refuses to accommodate students, and seems to pride herself all the time. DO NOT TAKE!!!!

The exams are based on really nitpicky concepts. Her lectures are boring. I hate the quizzes that start in the first 5 mins and just close, plus you never know when you will have a quiz. Lots of reading and just too much work
Really nitpicky grading from the professor. The class is relatively easy; it's just that the professor will point out every little thing "wrong" in your work and grade extremely subjectively.

This class was only difficult because of the professor. The information taught is genuinely interesting, but the way the professor is so hard on clarity/punctuation when forcing students to write in a time crunch is asinine. Would only take if interested in the INLS major/minor. Really hope she changes how she approaches this class.

analysis.name: Toni Dinardo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

Youcouldbring an indexcardfor everyquizandcheatsheet forthefinal.

This class is fairly easy, as there are not many assignments. The majority of the class is group projects, which make it more fun and interesting. Although class drags on and we often go off topic, Toni gives us everything we need to succeed in the class. I would definitely take this class for the english requirement.

Toni just speaks at you in class with language complexity that many students can't understand. She is chill but her class drags on and is just to get the requirement done. As a stem major, I couldn't recommend it less. Maybe if you're business you would enjoy it more. Or if you know about Lord of the Rings, as that's all she talks about.

Toni is a great and accommodating person, and cares for the wellbeing of us as students.  English 105i in the social sciences wasn't the most interesting for me as a STEM major, but Toni's class is very easy to follow along with regardless of your major.  I highly recommend!!

We covered all of the ENGL-105 curricula in the first month and spent the rest of the semester putting together conference papers. Toni gave us a lot of freedom, so I ended up having a great time researching a subject I had been interested in, but never had time to research before! If you have to take ENGL-105, take it with Toni!

analysis.name: Duane Deardorff
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 92 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I think Dr. Deardorff is a lovely person, and he seems very sweet outside of the context of PHYS-114. He is very condescending and snappy in lecture, and is not the most effective at teaching the material. Most of his class is self-taught with the help of TA office hours because the TAs seem very sympathetic about how the class is run.

The exams are graded well (lots partial), so it is possible to get an A. However, Deardorf is one of the most condescending and rude professors I have ever had. Would not be kind to students when they answered incorrectly in class. When 9% of the class got a question right on an exam he told us we needed to study more...

duane would be a great professional juggler. he is not a good professional professor. extremely condenscending in both emails and lectures and manages to make simple concepts confusing. had a different lecturer for two months and the class did better than previous semesters on the second exam.

Avoid the scale up classes for your own good.  Basically nothing is taught in these classes and you are responsible for not only teaching yourself all of the material outside of class, but also a maddening amount of short and long lab reports and homework assignments.  Class attendance is mandatory for some reason, despite being completely useless.

He does not seem to care for our success. We do much of the learning ourselves so he is essentially the placeholder that contributes relatively little to our understanding. The actual learning is done during the 3-hour lab sessions. Would not recommend the class but there is a very limited selection of instructors here who teach this, so no choice.

analysis.name: Daniel DiSalvo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor DiSalvo is awesome! The only reason I didn't rate him as a 5 is because I am personally not the biggest fan of the structure of the class. However, I know it could work very well for many others. Essentially, you read historical documents and take notes (not graded) outside of class and then spend the whole time in class discussing them.

Amazing professor! You can tell he really cares about his students and is willing to accommodate. The class is very discussion based but if you don't feel comfortable speaking up in class he gives multiple opportunities to get those points. He also gives multiple extra credit opportunities and helps students prepare for exams!

Dr. DiSalvo is a super cool guy and really knows American history and judicial history. Very informative class but could be a little dry in lectures. He clearly cared about his students and was easy to talk to and ask questions.

analysis.name: Diego Riveros-Iregui
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: This class was so unbearable. Everybody was taking this as either a focus capacity or to fulfill their data science minor. They wanted us to be so dedicated to the topic so bad but no one cared. Such a boring class and attendance matters. Started picking on me for no reason towards the end of the semester in a 200 person class. Don't recommend.

Honestly I dreaded going to this class. Professor was passive agressive and randomly called on us. The lectures were a bit boring to me. Definitely requires some studying for the exams as the material is pretty dense, but making a good grade in the class overall isn't too difficult. Most exams were very similar to the practice ones he posted.

Big class (~150), but this professor makes a boring subject interesting with his genuine passion and animated lectures. He asks lots of questions, so stay alert or he'll call you out. Tons of material, but his energy and lively teaching make it manageable. He's one of two instructors, and he clearly loves what he teaches. Great engaging instructor

Dr. Riveros-Iregui is so friendly and a very engaging professor. You can tell he wants his students to succeed in class and he'd specify on slides where they would be important in an exam. He gets upset when students don't focus in class or are distracted on their devices, and you get more out of class when you pay attention in lectures.

Seems like a chill guy, but lots of condescending comments. Blamed wifi. Expect you to devote your life to geography in a 100 level class for data science majors. THE WORLD DOESNT REVOLVE AROUND GEOGRAPHY. Expect you to come to class having done the readings but not doing that. So i just didn't go a lot of times. easy class though

analysis.name: Martina Di Francesco

review_highlights.comment: I have taken Martina for ITAL 101, 102, and 204 because she is THAT amazing. She is a caring instructor and makes class so much fun. She is so funny and really cares about you succeeding in the class. She is always making sure we are comfortable with the material and comfortable in her class. Can't recommend her more!
Martina is my favorite UNC professor. I changed my schedule to take ITAL 204 with her because she's that great. I learned so much from her and loved her class!! I can't recommend her enough!!

Martina is amazing and definitely one of the best professors you could get for any italian classes. The course is set up the same as 101 and 102 with homeworks due before each class, 4 tests, a small group project before each test, and two very easy quizzes in each unit. Would definitely recommend Martina to anyone taking italian!
She is so sweet! Never judgmental of your ability level & meets you where you are. If I could I would have taken her for all 3 levels.

Martina made learning a new language enjoyable and easy! I took 101 as a gen-ed but am seriously considering an Italian minor after taking her class. She goes out of her way to help comprehension and uses hilarious real world examples. Take Italian with Martina!!

analysis.name: Jennifer Diliberto
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I felt kind of patronized throughout this class, we were treated like children. Pretty project heavy,  but graded easily. Attendance was super important to your grade, felt like she thought her class was the only one that mattered.The class felt unorganized and had confusing instructions. She's a nice person, but not great for a college professor.

Dr. Diliberto is such a sweet and knowledgeable professor, but the class material often feels repetitive and grating. Class is pretty project and quiz-based. Quizzes are very specific. Projects have slightly unclear instructions. The professor is great to talk to outside of class. Overall, not a bad class, but not the most engaging.

The best teacher!! So kind and caring! Class was fun and engaging, and I learned SO much. Not hard to get an A. She is so knowledgeable on the topics and wants to talk to you about them! Go see her outside of class, you won't regret it! weekly online quizzes, a couple of projects, and a collaborative final.

Sweetest Professor ever! She clearly wants all of us to learn and gives encouraging, constructive feedback. This async class was very reasonable and very interesting. You do have 5 discussion zoom calls with other students, so just be aware of that going in if you're expecting a fully async class. Great class and I learned a lot!

Dr. Diliberto is so sweet and cares about her students! She was good about asking for feedback twice throughout the semester to see what she should change. Lots of fun group discussions but never forced to participate in front of the whole class. She encourages you to think outside of the box but sometimes can be vague, but easy grader regardless.

analysis.name: Dilshad Imon

analysis.name: Julie Dixon

review_highlights.comment: Very kind and sweet professor, but you won't learn a lot from her. She is truly the nicest prof ever though

I was startled by how friendly she was over Zoom and how much she genuinely cared about getting students into the PR world. She shared a lot of cool personal anecdotes, she's hella impressive. She used powerpoints every class but it feels we didnt really learn much in the end. I see it more like a career fair and less like a typical class.

The people who have not enjoyed Professor Dixon are too nit picky or not participatory in class. She is incredibly encouraging while being straight forward. She has a great amount of industry experience and her classes in my experience have proivded good experience I can put on a resume. Big fan.

Shawty loves talking about herself but actually so fun and such an easy class if you put in the effort. This was the first class I've taken at UNC that I got to meet people online and actually connect with them. Definitely a good class to balance out my others and Jules is so awesome. Everyone who hates on her doesn't know how to relax

I love Jules!! Each of her classes is definitely fun, and I truly did look forward to showing up every day. That said, I don't know how much I have learned from her...? I know lots about her personality, personal life, the people she knows, etc... but the bulk of my Hussman knowledge has definitely come from other professors. But fun & low-stress!

analysis.name: Dwayne Dixon

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Dixon is the most passionate lecturer and most well spoken professor I have had so far at UNC. Take his classes, he won't try to hurt your GPA, show what you have learned and you will be rewarded with a grade and some captivating lectures.

Dwayne is a great guy and the assignments you have are easy and graded leniently. However, he gets up there and preaches his political agenda which is kind of annoying. If you can deal with that though, it is definitely worth the GPA boost. The final is only worth 10% of your grade and the only reason he has one is because it is required.

Awful... the professor makes you feel super uncomfortable in class. Im not paying him for him to rant about his personal opinion on the political situation of the world. Definitely not a beginner's class, you need to have some basic experience with the material beforehand. DONT go to his office hours, he's incredibly judgy and rude.

Professor Dixon is a captivating lecturer who facilitates profound discussions during lecture. Although there is a lot of readings assigned, they aren't required if you go to lecture and pay attention. If you do the small amount of work he asks of you, you will be rewarded with great lectures and an A. This class is a great GPA boost/GenEd provider

Took this class in the spring, very easy class as long as you keep up with it. It can be TA-reliant, but I've never heard of somebody having a tough time in this class. Dwayne is definitely an interesting guy, but I'd say the people in these reviews trashing him are overreacting.

analysis.name: Dog Dick

I can not recommend someone better or more kind than Prof Howlett. He is truly such a caring and personable guy. 

He always checks up on his students, provides great feedback on assignments, and keeps class interesting. I have never felt that my time in his class was wasted. Take him for MEJO 153. Even if it is in the evening. Take him.
BEST PROFESSOR EVER PLS TAKE HIM! Kindest teacher and genuinely cares about you and your learning. Gives thorough feedback and is so understanding. I love going to his class!

If you have the chance to take Mejo 153 with Prof. Howlett DO IT. He's one of the best professors I've had at UNC. His extensive feedback on every paper was so helpful and I'm a better writer because of it. The class does have a lot of papers, but Howlett does his best to make every assignment interesting and a learning opportunity. He's awesome!

By far the best professor I have had at UNC! Prof. Howlett is an amazing teacher who made a generally tough course very enjoyable! There is a decent amount of writing, but it is very manageable. The lectures are super informative and are very helpful in becoming a better writer. Above all, he is super caring for his students and is very genuine!

analysis.name: Scott Duxbury
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Duxbury is incredibly kind and makes the homework very straightforward. I came in with no coding experience, and he makes everything doable. He's passionate, always willing to help, and his office hours are amazing. Plus, there's a ton of extra credit available.

i think you'd have to try to do bad in this class. Scott is a great prof - v caring, accessible, knowledgable, gives great feedback. i loved this class; it was genuinely interesting, and learned a lot w/out ever being stressed abt it. no exams, just reading quizzes (open note) and ~5 hw and a final project - all v doable w/out R/coding experience

Prof. Duxbury is such an amazing human being and lecturer. He's clearly knowledgeable and enjoys teaching. He introduced me to data science and motivated to pursue it as a major. Overall, take this class with him if you can! :)

Scott was an amazing professor. If you had any problems he was always available and throughout the course of the semester we would slowly chip away at our final. He gives great feedback and makes all the hw/quizzes very manageable. If you show up and do the work you will do fantastic. Highly recommend
Probably my favorite professor I've ever had at UNC. The class was a super easy A as well, definitely recommend!

analysis.name: Dylan Russell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dylan is super passionate about PA and it really shows in his teaching. He is super personable and one of the most kind professors I've had at UNC. Sometimes the content can be boring but Dylan definitely is not boring. The Service Learning component was one of my favorite parts of the course! I recommend for the SL requirement.

Dylan is very accessible and uses his connections to bring in great guest speakers; he assigns interesting material. The memos are not difficult, and he cares more about your final policy project being something you are interested in.
Professor Russell is great. You can tell he is passionate about what he teaches and truly cares about the success of his students. If you're in need of an EE credit course, look no further.

Professor Russell's class was my favorite by far this past semester!  He is a once in a lifetime professor.  His lectures were engaging and informative!  You can really see his passion for the public sector.  The feedback on assignments had excellent attention to detail.  He has solidified my interest in working for the public sector!

Dylan was a wonderful professor and is incredibly passionate about what he does. He definitely had a lot on his plate this semester, but always made himself available as a resource for his students. I learned so much in this course, and am now interested in pursuing a career in local government. The workload is manageable and relates to the course.

analysis.name: Dylan Thompson
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dylan is a great guy and teacher. He is enthusiastic and it is infectious. He always starts class with music and discussion about music and basketball often carry over into class. He gives very good lectures full of fun examples and pop culture references. He likes participation in class. He is not too harsh with grading and wants you to succeed.

Dylan is amazing. As someone who constantly asks questions and likes to engage in class, Dylan is always accommodating to my needs and everyone else. He is super easy to get along with and you'll never be bored during class. You will also learn very useful tasks that you'll be able to apply to other classes. This was my favorite class and professor

DYLAN IS THE MAN. Class usually consists of powerpoints or just all of us discussing a topic, but his keen sense of humor is able to make even the most arbitrary topics fun. He is really accessible out of class and willing to discuss with students to work on improving. I had a great time in this class even though it was a lot of writing at times.

Dylan always plays music before class starts and starts the class with funny conversation . He made writing seem enjoyable and always offered interesting feedback and perspectives. 10/10 would recommend him. I loved his class and would take him again if possible. His lectures are always entertaining and discussion in the class is always enjoyable.

Dylan is awesome!!! He always plays good music before class, he gives good feedback, and he makes a mandatory class like ENGL 105 enjoyable and valuable. He cares about his students and will have fun conversations with you. He also gives GREAT feedback, and if you use him as a resource, his class will really help you improve your writing!

analysis.name: Dylan Glotzer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Glotzer uses a blackboard during lecture; thus, you MUST come to class.  Moreover, he gives practice tests that are VERY similar to the actual tests.  Take the practice tests, tease out the main concepts, and practice questions related to those concepts.  If you do so, there is no reason to less than an A.  This class was SO easy.

Dylan is a grad student himself so he understands that students are busy and works with everyone's needs. He is super chill and you are not required to attend any lecture at all, it'd just be hard to pass if you didn't go and didn't have any stats background. Grades are only based off of nightly HW, 2 midterms and a final. Take him for this class.

Dylan is a good lecturer, and also a really understanding guy. He almost always gave extensions on the homework when more than a few people are struggling. He will even give individual extensions the homework- no questions asked. Exams are very similar to the practice tests he gives. Overall, he's a good choice for STOR 155, and funny as well.

Dylan is really awesome. Probably my favorite thing is that whenever anyone asks a question, he always responds "that's a great question." He never treats anyone like they are stupid even if it's kind of a dumb or repetitive question. Also super approachable, practice exams are nearly identical to actual, so those aren't bad.

Dylan is a goofy and awkward guy. That being said, he is very sweet and funny at times. He really cares about his students and always opens himself up for questions and help outside of class. He never tries to trick you on exams as they are usually from him practice exams. Easy web assign homework and class done on the blackboard.

analysis.name: Dylan Parker
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: You should be warned.  If you have a limited view of the world and you want to keep your views limited... do not take this class. Myself... I will never look at the world in the same way again.
WOW is all I can say. I am not a history buff, but this class made me a new person. I have never had a better teacher.
Wild Class!  I learned more from him about the history of the human race than from anyone else I have ever met.
Dr. Parker is one of the best teachers I have ever had. The class is not easy, but it is very fun!
Great Class.  It forces you to understand the way the world of man was formed.

analysis.name: Walter Bo Eberle
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Class consisted of discussions that he never offered feedback. Posts by students in the forum asking questions went unanswered, students also said emails went unanswered. Going into the final only the first discussion had been graded, nothing else.

Class consists of 1 weekly discussion post, a midterm, and a final paper. Super easy and he grades well, but hard to access outside of class especially since this class was asynchronous. Great TA though!
Bo rules. That is all. I only feel bad for him having to guide recitations where no one did the reading.

analysis.name: Patrick Eberlein
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Wow you need to get this guy. He is fantastic. I really pity the other folks in the other classes because they do not get the opportunity to experience the greatness of Pat Eberlein. I have never been happier with a professor/ teacher in my life. Fair homework, fair tests, useful lectures. He also is a funny and kind character as well.

Far and away my best professor. Really helpful whenever you ask. He really teaches the class well and his tests aren't too hard. He tells you that what is on the test is all in the homework. He's being completely honest. If you study the homework, you'll be all set for the test.

I loved having Professor Eberlein. His lectures are easy to follow, and he is so knowledgeable on the subject. I would highly, highly recommend him. Also had him for Math 233, which we was great for as well.
Very helpful teacher. Knows the material well and gives clear explanations. The difficulty in his class has more to do with the material than any deficiency in his teaching style.
Great professor! Super willing to help out on homework (which you will probably need)

analysis.name: Angela East
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Kind and approachable person who is accessible, definitely take advantage of that; class was WAY harder than it should have been. Lectures: extremely hard to follow, and it often felt like she didn't know how to teach the material. The content taught barely matched the midterms, if it weren't for the practice exams I would have failed the class.

Ms. East was very sweet. She genuinely cares for the success of her students. However, I feel like her teaching style was not the best, as lessons were not always taught in a clear manner. I feel concepts could have been explained better in a simpler way; it sometimes would feel overly complicated. Her practice exams were very helpful!

Extremely inexperienced when it comes to teaching. She grades very harsh and unfair, will take off multiple points for small mistakes. She does not allow you to discuss any exam grades with her. She has terrible handwriting, making lectures difficult to understand. Does not take anything serious, she found it funny that her class average was 70%.

Felt significantly underprepared. She was accessible outside of class, but was always behind on lectures with rushed complex content! A nice person, but this class was extremely difficult. Still inexperienced. Appreciated how she supported the class. Caution taking this class though. Take the good and bad ratings with a grain of salt.

Prof East is one of the most caring professors I've ever had, she teaches really well, she is mostly organised and super adaptable. If you're gonna take 110, take it with her, she actually understands what it's like to be a student and she's flexible, considerate and has the best dad jokes. She's such a sweetie

analysis.name: Connie Eble
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Eble was fine in the history portion of this class, but the difficulty of the class shot up when we reached old English. She expects you to know all about the grammar, but she doesn't explain it well at all. If you've had any old English before you'll probably be fine, if not, good luck. She's a tough grader, and not always clear in criteria.

I had Ms. Eble along with her colleague Ms. Brown for the freshman seminar "Interpreting the South from Manuscripts." Ms. Eble is a hard grader, but she will make your writing so much better. The class itself I found to be very interesting as it is completely discussion and raw-reading based.  My favorite class of the semester!

This is my second class with Eble and I'm enjoying it even more than the last. She's willing to work with you--if you have a problem, she'll show you grace! She's a lot of fun and extremely knowledgeable in her field. Plus, the classes she teaches are always very interesting.

she tends to over explain things, which makes her class pretty boring, but you hear the same thing so many times you won't need to study much at home. she is very knowledgeable and not strict with grades. she is very strict on attendance though

She was very boring.  One day it snowed and many students were missing.  She proceeded to take out the dictionary and for 1 1/2 hours, read words from the dictionary and talked about their origins.  A complete waste of my time!

analysis.name: Elaina Eakle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Enjoyed taking this class and it was easy. Not too many assignments. not a very harsh grader. she is very nice and cares about what she teaches. Movies watched were interesting and we'd have to complete a discussion post/group discussion about 2 films and write 1 tv show review. Exams were multiple choice and one short answer question.

I loved this class and Elaina was a great instructor! She genuinely cares about her students and encourages prioritizing your health over class. That being said you have to at least act like you care and go sometimes to get participation credit. The class was super interesting and looked at gender and sexuality in the context of current events!

Honestly all of her ratings are hyping her up but I didn't like her that much. The papers and tests were annoying and kinda hard in my opinion. You definitely have to try if you want an A she doesn't just hand them out. And just in general her vibe is kinda strange, monotone voice, and just seems like she would much rather be doing anything else.

It's not letting me select the correct class, but I took Comm 325 with Elaina. She is so sweet and also an extremely lenient grader, gladly grants extensions, and will do everything in her power to accommodate your needs if you just communicate. Lectures and exams are straightforward.

Elaina is amazing! For those taking her class virtually, she provides a textbook but her videos are great. Her tests are open note and easy A's (no time limit!). She gave me lots of feedback and met extra with me for our course paper (20%). She is super kind and really cares about her students. I would be ecstatic taking another course with her.

analysis.name: Teacher Earl
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Sends great pics in his emails!!! super entertaining guy..... the D he gave me turned into an A by doing super easy extra credit! he's so understanding and not as hard as you would think

Prof. Teacher Earl has a strange grading policy that saw me get a B- even tho I specifically requested a B+ at the beginning of the semester. I am not a smart boy, so the B- was fair. Great guy over all, and the only time I hated his class was when we had a substitute for the week

in love with every cell of his being. i wish I could take every class of his. thinking about applying to grad school at unc just so I can continue to see him. cannot recommend him enough! take a class with him, you will not regret it!

Teacher Earl truly got me out of my depressive episode. He brought so much light to my life, changed my whole view on the world through sociology. He is a beautiful person, not just inside, but on the outside too. <3 ;)
Teacher Earl loves to perform silly social experiments during class. Some of these include watching Hillybillies and the Crippled Camp. Interesting films with disturbing images.

analysis.name: Tyler Easterbrook
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Tough quizzes! BUT, he grades projects leniently. The projects are fun too; do well on them (and talk every now and then in class) to get at least an A-. Tyler himself is interesting and fun to talk to. He made it a point to meet w/ every student before every project, which ends up being really helpful and says a lot about him!

Easterbrook was a great teacher. Effort is a huge thing for him. If you work hard, you will get a good grade even if you didn't do everything perfect. His lectures were really interesting and applicable to life. There were only like 4 projects and some reading quizzes. Very chill.
I loved Tyler's class! He was the most engaging instructor/professor I had this semester tbh. The class was mostly project-based and he was very willing to work with us with deadlines.

analysis.name: Megan Eagen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Megan is a wonderful person. I had no experience or even much interest in Baroque Opera, but she made the topic and the class extremely interesting and engaging. She's extremely caring, and if she sees that you give a good effort, you will be rewarded. She helped me tremendously in office hours this semester and was really a fantastic professor.

Dr. Megan Eagen-Jones is an excellent professor. This was her first class in a large lecture hall, and she managed to keep things engaging. Her lectures are interesting, and she does a good job of highlighting the main points that she tests on. She genuinely cares about her students and offers really in depth feedback on the papers she grades.

I've never written one of these before but this teacher was so phenomenal I had to.  Megan is a fantastic proffesor who really knows her stuff.  She isn't out to trick you on the tests and gives very helpful quizzes.  If you give her a little effort anyone can get an easy A here.

There are pop quizzes, but they're not hard. Homework once a week. Best to do the readings (they're not long), but she goes over what you need to know in class. Really chill class, good pacing, ample opportunities for participation. She's really understanding. 10/10 recommend!

One of the best professors I've had at UNC. Her passion and interest in the material is clear, and that translates to clear, engaging lectures that touch on really interesting material. Approachable, friendly, and fair, she really does care about helping you succeed no matter your circumstances. If you have the choice, definitely take 255 with her.

analysis.name: Maria Martinez Echague
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: What a fantastic and considerate professor! Her lectures were pretty interesting (even more so when I did the readings) and I found her to be fair, kind, and incredibly intelligent. The midterm exam was not bad (just required some review) and the final project was really interesting. Loved this class and so much respect for this prof

Prof Echague is great! She is a little soft-spoken so when she lectured, I struggled to stay engaged, but for most of the class we spoke in small groups. The class had a 'read an article before class, talk about it in class' structure, but I did enjoy the videos she showed in class. No final, instead, a group presentation. Easy, interesting class.

I found this class so interesting and valuable. Prof. Ines is kind, knowledgeable, interesting and open to critique. She is such a great person and professor. I would really encourage anyone who takes this class to do the readings because they allow you to get so much more from the course. The readings also make studying for the midterm easier.

Very few good things to say about this course. Structure is extremely repetitive but easy; read an article at home, discuss it with a group the next day, repeat. The course material is so surface-level with such little room for open thinking or varying perspectives that I can't say I learned anything new. Prof is slow and inconsistent grader.

I loved this professor so much! I found the class to be really interesting and they provided a lot of great reading. As long as you know the jest of what is going on in the readings, you should be fine. She gave a couple of little assignments, two in-class essays, a midterm, and a final essay. Conversations in this class were always great also!
